# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform

## Customer Account

- This platform requires registration to use any features (no guest browsing)
- Customers sign up with email and password
- Customers log in with email and password
- Customers can change their password
- Customers can delete their account
- When a customer deletes their account:
  - Their profile information is deleted
  - Their orders and order history are preserved (for seller records and legal purposes)
  - Their reviews are preserved but shown as "deleted user"

## Customer Profile

- Each customer has a profile with: display name and phone number
- Customers can edit their display name and phone number

## Address Management

- Customers can add multiple shipping addresses
- Each address has: recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state/province, postal code, country
- Customers can edit their addresses
- Customers can delete their addresses
- Customers can set one address as the default shipping address

## Seller Account

- Sellers sign up with email and password
- Sellers log in with email and password
- Sellers can change their password
- Seller accounts require administrator approval before they can sell
- Sellers can view their approval status (pending, approved, rejected)
- If rejected, sellers can view the rejection reason
- Rejected sellers can submit a new registration request
- Sellers can delete their account only if:
  - They have no pending orders (paid or shipped status)
  - They have no pending cancellation or refund requests
- When a seller deletes their account:
  - Their products are deleted from listings
  - Order history and snapshots are preserved
  - Their shop name in past orders is preserved

## Seller Profile

- Each seller has a profile with: shop name, shop description, and logo image
- Sellers can edit their shop name, description, and logo
- Every edit creates a snapshot
- Customers can view seller profiles

## Categories

- Products are organized into categories
- Categories can have subcategories (one level of nesting only)
- Each category has: name and description
- Categories are created and managed by administrators only
- Customers can browse the list of all categories
- Customers can view products within a category

## Snapshot Principle

- This is a platform where money is exchanged, so all data modifications must be recorded
- Whenever editable data is modified, a snapshot is created to preserve the previous state
- Snapshots record: when the change was made, what was changed, and the values before and after
- Snapshots are immutable and cannot be deleted
- Snapshots can be viewed by relevant parties (owners, administrators) for dispute resolution

**Product Snapshot Structure**
- When a product is edited, a product snapshot is created
- The product snapshot includes all product fields (name, description, category, base price, images)
- The product snapshot also includes snapshots of all variants at that moment (product-snapshot → product-snapshot-SKU)
- This preserves the complete state of a product and its variants at any point in time

**Snapshot applies to:**
- Products (all fields including images)
- Product variants (SKU code, option values, price)
- Seller profiles (shop name, description, logo)
- Order items (product, variant, and seller profile at time of purchase)
- Reviews (rating, text content)
- Cancellation requests (reason, status changes)
- Refund requests (reason, status changes)

## Products

- Sellers can create products
- Every product has:
  - Name (required)
  - Description (required)
  - Category (required, can select a subcategory)
  - Base price (required)
- Products belong to the seller who created them
- Sellers can edit their own products
- Every edit creates a snapshot
- Sellers can delete their own products only if:
  - There are no pending order items (paid or shipped status) for any variant of the product
  - There are no pending cancellation or refund requests for any variant of the product
- Deleting a product also deletes all its variants and inventory records
- Deleted products no longer appear in search or category listings
- Sellers can view snapshots of their own products
- Administrators can view snapshots of any product
- Snapshots are preserved even after product deletion

## Product Images

- Sellers can upload multiple images for each product
- Images can be reordered (first image is the main/thumbnail image)
- Sellers can delete images from their products
- Image changes are included in product snapshots

## Product Variants (SKU)

- A product can have multiple variants
- Each variant represents a specific combination of options (e.g., "Red / Large", "Blue / Small")
- Each variant has:
  - SKU code (unique identifier, required)
  - Option values (e.g., color: "Red", size: "Large")
  - Price (can override the base price, optional)
  - Stock quantity (required, starts at 0)
- Sellers can add variants to their products
- Sellers can edit variants (SKU code, option values, price)
- Every variant edit creates a snapshot
- Sellers can delete variants only if:
  - There are no pending order items (paid or shipped status) for that variant
  - There are no pending cancellation or refund requests for that variant
- A product must have at least one variant to be purchasable
- Products with no variants are visible in search but shown as "unavailable"

## Inventory Management

- Each variant has its own stock quantity
- Stock quantity is managed through inventory history records (not snapshots)
- Each inventory record contains: quantity change (positive for restocking, negative for orders/adjustments), reason, and timestamp
- Current stock is calculated by summing all inventory records
- Sellers can add inventory (restock) with a quantity and reason
- Sellers can subtract inventory (adjustment/loss) with a quantity and reason
- Order placement automatically creates a negative inventory record
- Order cancellation/refund automatically creates a positive inventory record
- Sellers can view the full inventory history of each variant
- When stock reaches 0, the variant is shown as "out of stock"
- Out of stock variants cannot be added to cart

## Product Search

- Customers can search products by name
- Search results show products from all sellers
- Search results are paginated
- Customers can filter search results by:
  - Category
  - Price range (minimum and maximum)
  - In-stock only
- Customers can sort search results by:
  - Newest first
  - Price (low to high)
  - Price (high to low)

## Product Listing

- When viewing a list of products (search results, category page), each product shows:
  - Main image (thumbnail)
  - Name
  - Base price (or price range if variants have different prices)
  - Seller shop name
  - Average rating (if reviews exist)

## Product Detail Page

- Customers can view a single product's full details
- The page shows:
  - All images
  - Name and description
  - Category
  - Seller shop name (links to seller profile)
  - All available variants with prices and stock status
  - Average rating and total review count
  - All reviews

## Wishlist

- Customers can add products to their wishlist
- Customers can view their wishlist
- The wishlist is paginated
- Wishlist shows products (not specific variants)
- Customers can remove products from their wishlist
- If a product is deleted by the seller, it is automatically removed from all wishlists

## Shopping Cart

- Customers can add variants to their cart (must select a specific variant, not just a product)
- When adding to cart, customers specify the quantity
- If the same variant is already in the cart, the quantities are combined (not added as a separate line)
- Customers can view their cart
- Cart shows each item with: product name, variant options, price, quantity, and subtotal
- Customers can change the quantity of items in their cart
- Customers can remove items from their cart
- Cart shows the total price of all items
- If a variant's stock is less than the cart quantity, a warning is shown
- If a variant is deleted or out of stock, it is marked as unavailable in the cart

## Checkout

- Customers can proceed to checkout from their cart
- Unavailable items cannot be checked out
- Customers must select a shipping address (or use default)
- Customers can review the order summary before placing the order:
  - List of items with prices
  - Shipping address
  - Total price
- Once an order is placed, the shipping address cannot be changed

## Payment

- After reviewing, customers confirm and place the order
- Payment is processed (assume external payment gateway integration)
- Payment can succeed or fail
- If payment fails, the order is not created and customers can retry
- If payment succeeds, the order is created

## Order Creation

- When an order is placed successfully:
  - Stock quantities are decreased for each purchased variant
  - Items are removed from the customer's cart
  - An order record is created
  - Each purchased variant becomes an order item with status "paid"
  - A snapshot of each purchased product and variant is saved with the order item (preserves product name, description, variant options, and price at the time of purchase)
  - A snapshot of each seller's profile is saved with the order item (preserves shop name and logo at the time of purchase)

## Order Structure

- An order contains one or more order items
- Each order item represents a purchased product variant with a quantity
- If a customer buys 3 of the same variant, it becomes one order item with quantity 3
- Order items can be from different sellers
- Each order item has its own status
- Each order item can be individually cancelled or refunded
- Order items are grouped into shipments when shipped (see Shipping and Tracking)

## Order History

- Customers can view a list of all their orders
- The list is paginated and sorted by newest first
- Each order in the list shows: order number, date, total price, and overall order status
- Customers can view the full details of an order:
  - List of items with: product name, variant, quantity, price, and item status
  - Shipping address
  - List of shipments with tracking information (each shipment shows which items are included)

## Order Status

**Order Item Status**
- Each item in an order has its own status
- Item statuses:
  - Paid: payment completed, waiting for seller to ship
  - Shipped: seller has shipped the item
  - Delivered: item has been delivered
  - Cancelled: item was cancelled
  - Refunded: item was refunded

**Order Status**
- The overall order status is derived from its items
- If all items are paid → order is "paid"
- If any item is shipped (and none delivered yet) → order is "shipped"
- If all items are delivered → order is "delivered"
- If all items are cancelled → order is "cancelled"
- If all items are refunded → order is "refunded"
- Mixed states (e.g., some delivered, some refunded) → order is "partially completed"

## Shipping and Tracking

**Shipment Concept**
- A shipment is a package sent by a seller
- A shipment can contain one or more order items from the same seller
- Different sellers always ship separately (different shipments)
- A seller can choose to ship items individually or bundle multiple items into one shipment

**Shipping Process**
- Sellers can view order items for their products that need shipping
- When shipping, sellers select one or more of their items to include in a shipment
- Sellers enter tracking information for the shipment (carrier name, tracking number)
- All items in the same shipment share the same tracking information
- When a shipment is created, all items in it change to status "shipped"

**Delivery Confirmation**
- Customers can view tracking information for each shipment
- Customers confirm delivery per shipment (not per item)
- When the customer confirms delivery, all items in that shipment change to status "delivered"
- If the customer does not confirm, items automatically change to "delivered" after 14 days from shipping

## Order Cancellation

- Cancellation is handled per order item, not per entire order
- Customers can request cancellation for individual items with status "paid" (not yet shipped)
- Cancellation requests include a reason (text)
- The seller of that item can approve or reject the cancellation request
- When a seller responds, a snapshot of the request state is created
- If approved, that item is cancelled and refund is processed for that item only
- Cancelled items restore their stock quantities (via inventory record)
- The remaining items in the order continue processing normally
- If all items in an order are cancelled, the entire order status becomes "cancelled"

## Refund Requests

- Refund is handled per order item, not per entire order
- Customers can request a refund for individual items with status "delivered"
- Refund requests include a reason (text)
- Refund can be requested within 7 days of that item being delivered
- The seller of that item can approve or reject the refund request
- When a seller responds, a snapshot of the request state is created
- If approved, that item is refunded
- Refunded items restore their stock quantities (via inventory record)
- The remaining items in the order are unaffected
- If all items in an order are refunded, the entire order status becomes "refunded"

## Reviews and Ratings

- Customers can write a review for products they have purchased
- A review can only be written after that item's status is "delivered"
- Customers can write one review per product per order
- Each review has:
  - Rating (1 to 5 stars, required)
  - Text content (optional)
- Reviews are displayed on the product detail page
- Reviews are sorted by newest first
- Customers can edit their own reviews
- Every review edit creates a snapshot
- Customers can delete their own reviews (but snapshots are preserved)
- Product's average rating is calculated from all non-deleted reviews

## Seller Dashboard

- Sellers can view a summary of their shop:
  - Total number of products
  - Total number of order items (for their products)
  - Number of pending cancellation requests
  - Number of pending refund requests
- Sellers can view a list of all order items for their products
- Sellers can filter order items by status

## Administrator System

**Becoming an Administrator**
- Any user (customer or seller) can submit a request to become an administrator
- The request includes a reason (text)
- Super administrators can view the list of pending requests
- Super administrators can approve or reject requests
- When approved, the user becomes a regular administrator

**Administrator Grades**
- There are two grades: regular administrator and super administrator
- Super administrators can promote regular administrators to super administrator
- Super administrators can demote other super administrators to regular administrator
- Super administrators cannot demote themselves

**Seller Management**
- Administrators can view the list of pending seller approvals
- Administrators can approve or reject seller registrations
- When rejecting, administrators must provide a reason
- Rejected sellers can submit a new registration request
- Administrators can suspend seller accounts
- When a seller is suspended:
  - Their products are hidden from search and category listings
  - Their products cannot be purchased
  - They can still process existing orders (ship items, respond to cancellation/refund requests)
  - They cannot create new products or edit existing products
- Administrators can unsuspend seller accounts (products become visible again)

**Category Management**
- Administrators can create categories and subcategories
- Administrators can edit category names and descriptions
- Administrators can delete categories (products in deleted categories become uncategorized)

**Product Oversight**
- Administrators can view all products on the platform
- Administrators can view snapshots of any product
- Administrators can delete any product (for policy violations)

**Order Oversight**
- Administrators can view all orders on the platform
- Administrators can force-cancel individual items or entire orders (refunds the customer, restores stock)
- Administrators can force-refund individual items or entire orders

**User Management**
- Administrators can view all customer accounts
- Administrators can ban customers (banned customers cannot log in)
- Administrators can unban customers
- Administrators can view all seller accounts
- Administrators can ban sellers (banned sellers cannot log in, existing orders remain)

operations.specification: Implementation: Generate a new JWT access token and refresh token pair for an unauthenticated visitor. Create a guest session record in the database with the refresh token hash, expiration timestamps, and client metadata. Return both tokens in the response. No input credentials required since this creates a temporary anonymous session. The access token should have a short expiration (e.g., 15 minutes) and the refresh token longer (e.g., 7 days) to allow session persistence.
operations.description:
Creates a new guest session for unauthenticated visitors.

This endpoint allows unauthenticated visitors to obtain a temporary JWT session before accessing registration or login endpoints. The platform requires authentication for all features, so guests must first establish a session token to proceed with account creation.

The operation generates fresh access and refresh tokens, stores the session record in the database with expiration timestamps, and returns the tokens to the client. The returned access token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent API calls.

This is typically the first API call made by a visitor to the platform. Once a guest has tokens, they can use them to access the customer or seller registration endpoints.

requestBody.description: Optional metadata for the guest session creation. No credentials are required for guest sessions.

responseBody.description: The guest session tokens containing access token and refresh token for subsequent authenticated requests.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Implementation: Validate the provided refresh token against the guest_sessions table. Check that the token is not expired and matches a valid session record. Generate a new access token and optionally rotate the refresh token for security. Update the session record with new token hashes and expiration timestamps. Return the new token pair. If the refresh token is invalid or expired, return a 401 error requiring the client to call join again.
operations.description:
Refreshes an existing guest session with new access and refresh tokens.

This endpoint allows guest clients to extend their session validity when the access token expires. The client must provide a valid refresh token obtained from the initial join response or previous refresh response.

The operation validates the refresh token against the stored session record, generates new token pairs, updates the session record with new expiration timestamps, and returns fresh tokens. Token rotation may be implemented for enhanced security.

If the refresh token is invalid, expired, or revoked, the operation returns a 401 error and the client must call join again to establish a new guest session.

requestBody.description: The refresh token from the existing guest session to exchange for new tokens.

responseBody.description: The new guest session tokens containing fresh access token and refresh token for continued authenticated access.

Create customer record with email and password_hash. Generate JWT access and refresh tokens. Create session record in ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions with ip, href, referrer, and expiration timestamp. Return tokens in IEcommerceMallCustomer.IAuthorized response.
operations.description:
Register a new customer account with email and password.

Creates a new customer record in the ecommerce_mall_customers table with the provided email address and hashed password. Validates that the email address is unique across all customer accounts. Upon successful registration, establishes a new authenticated session and returns JWT access and refresh tokens.

The session is recorded in ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions with connection context including IP address, referring page, and timestamps for security auditing. Customers can immediately use their credentials to access protected endpoints after registration.

This endpoint establishes the customer's identity in the system and issues authentication credentials for subsequent API access.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens including access token and refresh token for the newly registered customer session.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Implementation notes: Look up customer by email in ecommerce_mall_customers table. Verify password_hash matches provided password using secure comparison. Check account is not soft deleted (deleted_at is null). Reject if credentials invalid. Generate JWT access and refresh tokens. Create session record in ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions tracking connection context. Return tokens in IEcommerceMallCustomer.IAuthorized response.
operations.description:
Authenticate an existing customer with email and password credentials.

Validates the provided email address and password against the ecommerce_mall_customers table. Uses secure password hashing comparison to verify credentials. Rejects authentication if the email is not found, password does not match, or the account has been soft deleted.

Upon successful authentication, generates new JWT access and refresh tokens and creates a session record in ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions capturing the connection context (IP address, referring URL, timestamps) for security monitoring.

The returned access token must be included in subsequent API requests via the Authorization header. The refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens when the current one expires.

requestBody.description: Customer login credentials containing email address and password for authentication.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens including access token and refresh token for the authenticated customer session.

Look up associated customer from ecommerce_mall_customers table. Verify customer account is active (not deleted). Generate new JWT access token with fresh expiration. Optionally rotate refresh token for security. Return new tokens in IEcommerceMallCustomer.IAuthorized response.
operations.description:
Refresh an expired or soon-to-expire access token using a valid refresh token.

Accepts a refresh token previously issued during login or registration and returns a new access token without requiring the customer to re-enter credentials. Validates the refresh token against the session records and verifies the associated customer account remains active.

For enhanced security, this operation may also issue a new refresh token (token rotation) and invalidate the previous one to prevent replay attacks. The refresh token itself is stored in the ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions table with expiration tracking.

Use this endpoint when the access token expires (typically returns 401 Unauthorized) to maintain the customer's session without interrupting their workflow.

requestBody.description: Token refresh request containing the refresh token obtained from previous login or registration.

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens including fresh access token and potentially new refresh token for continued session.

Create session record in ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions capturing IP, href, referrer from request headers. Return tokens and seller info. Error scenarios: duplicate email (409), invalid email format (400), password too weak (400).
operations.description:
Register a new seller account on the platform. Sellers must provide a unique email address and password to create an account. Upon successful registration, the seller account is created with pending approval status and requires administrator review before products can be listed. The operation creates a seller registration application that tracks the approval workflow.

The registration process validates email uniqueness, enforces password strength requirements, and securely hashes the password using bcrypt. A JWT access token and refresh token are issued upon successful registration, allowing immediate authentication while awaiting approval.

Seller accounts with pending status can log in but cannot create products or list items for sale until an administrator approves the registration.

Check that account is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null). Generate new JWT access and refresh tokens. Create session record in ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions with connection metadata (IP, href, referrer). Return tokens and seller info including approval_status. Error scenarios: invalid credentials (401), account not found (401), account deleted (401).
operations.description:
Authenticate an existing seller using email and password credentials. This operation validates the provided credentials against the stored password hash and establishes a new JWT authentication session.

Upon successful authentication, the system issues fresh access and refresh tokens and records the session with connection metadata (IP address, origin URL, referrer) for security auditing. The response includes the seller's current approval status, which determines whether they can list products or must wait for administrator approval.

Soft-deleted accounts cannot log in. The operation supports the complete authentication flow for approved, pending, and rejected sellers to check their account status.

requestBody.description: Seller login credentials containing email and password for authentication

responseBody.description: Authenticated seller session with JWT access token, refresh token, and seller account details including approval status

Verify session belongs to the authenticated seller and has not expired. Generate new JWT access token with updated expiration. Optionally rotate refresh token for security. Update session record with new token information and extended expiration. Return new tokens and seller info. Error scenarios: invalid refresh token (401), expired session (401), seller not found (401).
operations.description:
Renew an expired or nearly-expired JWT access token using a valid refresh token. This operation extends the seller's authenticated session without requiring re-entry of credentials.

The refresh token is validated against the active sessions stored in the ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions table. Upon successful validation, a new access token is issued with a fresh expiration timestamp. The session record is updated to reflect the continued activity.

This operation is essential for maintaining long-lived sessions while adhering to JWT security best practices through short-lived access tokens and periodic refresh.

requestBody.description: Token refresh request containing the refresh token to exchange for new access credentials

responseBody.description: Refreshed seller session with new JWT access token, refresh token, and seller account details

operations.specification: Join operation for administrator accounts. This is typically used when a user (customer or seller) has been approved as an administrator through the AdminPromotionRequest flow. The operation validates the email and password match an existing admin record with 'active' status. Upon successful validation, creates a new session in ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions with JWT access token and refresh token. Capture client metadata (ip, href, referrer) for security auditing. Hash the provided password using BCrypt and compare against password_hash. Set token expiration based on configuration (e.g., access token 15 minutes, refresh token 30 days). operations.description:
Administrator join operation. Administrators are created through the promotion request flow (AdminPromotionRequest) approved by super administrators, not through public registration. This operation authenticates an existing admin account using email and password credentials.

Validates the email exists in ecommerce_mall_admins, verifies the BCrypt password_hash matches the provided password, and confirms the account status is 'active' (suspended or banned accounts cannot authenticate). Administrators have two privilege grades: 'regular' (standard admin permissions) and 'super_admin' (can promote/demote other admins).

Upon successful authentication, creates a new session record in ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions with JWT tokens (access and refresh), captures connection metadata (IP address, page URL, referrer) for security audit trails, and returns the authorization tokens with admin profile information.

Verify BCrypt password_hash. On success, create a session in ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions with JWT tokens including: access token (short-lived, e.g., 15 min) and refresh token (long-lived, e.g., 30 days). Capture IP, href, referrer from request headers for security audit. Set expired_at based on refresh token lifetime. Return IEcommerceMallAdmin.IAuthorized containing tokens and admin profile (id, email, grade, status, nickname).
operations.description:
Administrator login operation. Authenticates administrators using email and password credentials stored in the ecommerce_mall_admins table.

The operation performs multiple validations: verifies the email exists, checks the account status is 'active' (suspended or banned administrators cannot log in), and validates the password against the BCrypt password_hash. Administrators have two grades: 'regular' (standard admin with seller approval, category management, and oversight permissions) and 'super_admin' (additional privileges to promote/demote administrators and approve admin promotion requests).

Upon successful authentication, creates a session record in ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions with JWT access and refresh tokens. Captures security metadata including IP address, referring URL (href), and HTTP referrer for audit trail purposes. Returns the authorization tokens along with the administrator's profile information.

Look up the session by matching the token and ensure it has not expired (expired_at > now()). On valid token, issue a new access token with updated expiration time. The refresh token itself may be rotated (optional security practice) or kept the same. Update the session record if token rotation is implemented. Return IEcommerceMallAdmin.IAuthorized with the new access token. If the session has expired or the token is invalid, return 401 Unauthorized.
operations.description:
Token refresh operation for administrator authentication. Allows administrators to obtain a new access token without re-entering credentials by presenting a valid refresh token.

The operation validates the provided refresh token against the ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions table, checking that the session exists and has not expired (expired_at timestamp is in the future). The refresh token is linked to the administrator via the admin_id foreign key relationship.

Upon successful validation, generates a new JWT access token with fresh expiration time. Implementing token rotation (issuing a new refresh token and invalidating the old one) is recommended for enhanced security but optional. Returns IEcommerceMallAdmin.IAuthorized containing the new access token, the refresh token (new or existing), and the administrator's profile information.

If the session has expired or the token is invalid/not found, returns 401 Unauthorized error requiring the administrator to log in again.

requestBody.description: Refresh token request containing the refresh token to exchange for a new access token.

responseBody.description: Authorization response with new JWT access token, the refresh token (rotated or original), and administrator profile information.

operations.specification: Super administrator registration operation. Creates a new super admin account with email and password. Implementation steps: 1) Validate request body contains email and password meeting business rules (email format, password complexity). 2) Check email uniqueness against ecommerce_mall_super_admins table - reject if exists. 3) Hash password using secure algorithm (bcrypt/Argon2). 4) Generate UUID for new record. 5) Insert into ecommerce_mall_super_admins with grade='super_admin', created_at/updated_at current timestamp. 6) Generate JWT access and refresh tokens. 7) Create session record in ecommerce_mall_super_admin_sessions with token metadata (IP, href, referrer from request context, created_at, expired_at). 8) Return IEcommerceMallSuperAdmin.IAuthorized containing tokens and super admin identity.
operations.description:
Register a new super administrator account.

Creates a new super administrator account with email-based authentication. The super administrator represents the highest privilege level in the platform hierarchy with abilities to approve admin promotion requests, promote/demote administrators, and manage the admin hierarchy.

Email must be unique across all super admin accounts. Password is securely hashed before storage. Upon successful registration, a JWT session is established with both access and refresh tokens returned. The session metadata including IP address and request context is recorded for audit purposes.

This operation is available publicly for initial super admin creation and requires no authentication.

requestBody.description: Super administrator registration credentials containing email and password for new account creation.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and super administrator identity returned upon successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Super administrator login operation. Validates credentials and establishes session. operations.description:
Authenticate a super administrator with email and password credentials.

Validates the provided email and password against the stored credentials in the ecommerce_mall_super_admins table. Only active accounts (not soft deleted) can authenticate. The email field is unique per account and serves as the login identifier.

Upon successful credential validation, a new JWT session is established. Both access and refresh tokens are generated and returned. The session is recorded in the ecommerce_mall_super_admin_sessions table with metadata including client IP address, page URL, and referrer for security monitoring. Previous sessions remain valid until they expire.

This operation is publicly accessible and requires no prior authentication.

requestBody.description: Super administrator login credentials containing email and password for authentication.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and super administrator identity returned upon successful login.

The operation verifies the associated session exists in ecommerce_mall_super_admin_sessions and that the super administrator account remains active (not soft deleted). This enables continuous access management while maintaining security through token rotation.

This operation is publicly accessible and requires no prior authentication header - the refresh token itself serves as the authentication credential in the request body.

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens returned upon successful token refresh.

operations.specification: Implementation: Generate a new JWT access token and refresh token pair for an unauthenticated visitor. Create a guest session record in the database with the refresh token hash, expiration timestamps, and client metadata. Return both tokens in the response. No input credentials required since this creates a temporary anonymous session. The access token should have a short expiration (e.g., 15 minutes) and the refresh token longer (e.g., 7 days) to allow session persistence.
operations.description:
Creates a new guest session for unauthenticated visitors.

This endpoint allows unauthenticated visitors to obtain a temporary JWT session before accessing registration or login endpoints. The platform requires authentication for all features, so guests must first establish a session token to proceed with account creation.

The operation generates fresh access and refresh tokens, stores the session record in the database with expiration timestamps, and returns the tokens to the client. The returned access token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent API calls.

This is typically the first API call made by a visitor to the platform. Once a guest has tokens, they can use them to access the customer or seller registration endpoints.

requestBody.description: Optional metadata for the guest session creation. No credentials are required for guest sessions.

responseBody.description: The guest session tokens containing access token and refresh token for subsequent authenticated requests.

Generate a new access token and optionally rotate the refresh token for security. Update the session record with new token hashes and expiration timestamps. Return the new token pair. If the refresh token is invalid or expired, return a 401 error requiring the client to call join again.
operations.description:
Refreshes an existing guest session with new access and refresh tokens.

This endpoint allows guest clients to extend their session validity when the access token expires. The client must provide a valid refresh token obtained from the initial join response or previous refresh response.

The operation validates the refresh token against the stored session record, generates new token pairs, updates the session record with new expiration timestamps, and returns fresh tokens. Token rotation may be implemented for enhanced security.

If the refresh token is invalid, expired, or revoked, the operation returns a 401 error and the client must call join again to establish a new guest session.

requestBody.description: The refresh token from the existing guest session to exchange for new tokens.

responseBody.description: The new guest session tokens containing fresh access token and refresh token for continued authenticated access.

Register a new customer account with email and password.

The session is recorded in ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions with connection context including IP address, referring page, and timestamps for security auditing. Customers can immediately use their credentials to access protected endpoints after registration.

This endpoint establishes the customer's identity in the system and issues authentication credentials for subsequent API access.

Upon successful authentication, generates new JWT access and refresh tokens and creates a session record in ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions capturing the connection context (IP address, referring URL, timestamps) for security monitoring.

operations.description:
Refresh an expired or soon-to-expire access token using a valid refresh token.

Accepts a refresh token previously issued during login or registration and returns a new access token without requiring the customer to re-enter credentials. Validates the refresh token against the session records and verifies the associated customer account remains active.

For enhanced security, this operation may also issue a new refresh token (token rotation) and invalidate the previous one to prevent replay attacks. The refresh token itself is stored in the ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions table with expiration tracking.

Use this endpoint when the access token expires (typically returns 401 Unauthorized) to maintain the customer's session without interrupting their workflow.

The operation creates a seller registration application that tracks the approval workflow.

The registration process validates email uniqueness, enforces password strength requirements, and securely hashes the password using bcrypt. A JWT access token and refresh token are issued upon successful registration, allowing immediate authentication while awaiting approval.

Seller accounts with pending status can log in but cannot create products or list items for sale until an administrator approves the registration.

Administrators have two privilege grades: 'regular' (standard admin permissions) and 'super_admin' (can promote/demote other admins).

Upon successful authentication, creates a new session record in ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions with JWT tokens (access and refresh), captures connection metadata (IP address, page URL, referrer) for security audit trails, and returns the authorization tokens with admin profile information.

Returns the authorization tokens along with the administrator's profile information.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of all customer accounts for administrative oversight.

This operation provides administrators with comprehensive search capabilities to browse the complete customer base. It supports filtering by partial email matching, account status (active or banned), and registration date ranges. The response includes customer summary information optimized for list displays, showing essential identification and status information without exposing sensitive details.

Results are paginated with configurable page sizes and support cursor-based navigation for efficient browsing of large customer databases. Sorting options include newest first, email alphabetical order, and account status grouping.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_customers table with pagination and filtering support.

Apply search filters:
- email: Partial string match (LIKE query with wildcards)
- accountStatus: Exact match filtering for 'active' or 'banned' status
- registrationDateRange: Date range filter on created_at field
- displayName: Partial match on related CustomerProfile.display_name

Validate that the requesting actor has admin role before executing query.

Use cursor-based pagination (limit/after) for efficient large dataset navigation.

Join with ecommerce_mall_customer_profiles to include display name in results.
Exclude soft-deleted accounts from results unless explicitly requested.

Return IPageIEcommerceMallCustomer.ISummary with:
- customer id and email
- profile display name
- account status
- registration timestamp
- total order count (aggregated from related orders)

responseBody.description: Paginated list of customer account summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering customer accounts

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific customer account.

This operation returns the complete customer record identified by the provided customerId UUID. The response includes the customer's email address, account creation timestamp, and last update timestamp.

For security reasons, sensitive fields such as password hash are not included in the response. The deleted_at field indicates whether the customer account has been soft-deleted.

This endpoint is typically used by customers viewing their own account details or by administrators performing account oversight. Access control ensures customers can only view their own data unless they have administrative privileges.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_customers table by primary key id matching the customerId path parameter.

Return fields: id, email, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at.

Security consideration: Exclude password_hash from the response to prevent credential exposure.

Error handling:
- Return 404 Not Found if no customer exists with the given customerId
- Return 403 Forbidden if the requesting customer attempts to access another customer's data without admin privileges

The deleted_at field being non-null indicates a soft-deleted account where orders and reviews are preserved per business requirements.

responseBody.description: Complete customer account information

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the customer account (global scope)

operations.description:
Update the authenticated customer's profile information.

This operation allows customers to modify their public-facing profile data including display name and phone number. Both fields are editable throughout the account lifetime and changes take effect immediately upon saving.

The system verifies that the authenticated customer is modifying their own profile. Profile edits do not create snapshots as profile information is not subject to the snapshot principle that applies to transactional data.

If the submitted data fails validation (e.g., invalid phone number format), the request is rejected with specific validation error details.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Validate the authenticated customer's identity from the session. Verify the customer has a profile (created automatically during registration). Validate the request body fields: display name (string, optional for update), phone number (string, must be valid format). Update the profile record in ecommerce_mall_customers table. Return the updated profile with current values. Handle validation errors by returning 400 with specific field errors. Handle authentication errors by returning 401 if no valid session exists.

responseBody.description: The updated customer profile with current display name and phone number values

requestBody.description: Profile update data containing fields to modify (display name and/or phone number)

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of customer authentication sessions.

This operation provides session history retrieval with advanced filtering capabilities including creation date ranges, expiration status, and connection context filters. Customers can view their own active and expired sessions to monitor account access and security.

Sessions include connection metadata such as IP address, referrer URL, and creation timestamp. Expired sessions are retained for security auditing purposes. Results are paginated with cursor-based navigation for efficient browsing of large session histories.

Requires authentication. Customers can only access their own sessions. Administrators may have broader access depending on implementation policies.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions table with pagination and filtering.

Authorization: Verify authenticated customer can only access sessions where ecommerce_mall_customer_id matches their own customer ID. Administrators may bypass this restriction based on role.

Filtering support:
- created_at date range (from/to)
- expired_at date range for expired sessions
- expiration status filter (active only, expired only, or all)
- ip address partial matching for security analysis

Pagination: Use cursor-based pagination with created_at as the cursor field for consistent ordering. Support configurable page sizes (default 20, max 100).

Sorting: Primary sort by created_at DESC (newest first), secondary sort by id for stability.

Response fields include: id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at, and a flag indicating if the session is currently active (expired_at > now).

Do not include sensitive token data in the response.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of customer session summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering customer sessions

The ownership verification is performed before any update is applied. If the address does not belong to the requesting customer, the system will respond as if the address does not exist (to prevent address ID enumeration attacks). The system logs any unauthorized access attempts for security monitoring purposes.

After a successful update, the address will reflect the new information in the customer's address book for future order shipments. This update does NOT affect addresses already associated with placed orders, which maintain their original information for record-keeping purposes.

1. Verify the authenticated customer's identity from the session

6. Validate all required fields are present in the request body: recipientName, phoneNumber, streetAddress, city, stateOrProvince, postalCode, country
7. Execute the update with the new field values

9. Handle edge cases: non-existent address ID, invalid UUID format, missing required fields

operations.description:
Permanently delete a customer's shipping address.

This operation removes the specified address from the customer's address book. The address will no longer be available for selection during checkout.

**Ownership Verification**: The system verifies that the address belongs to the authenticated customer. If the address does not belong to the customer, the request is rejected with a response identical to a non-existent address to prevent address enumeration attacks.

**Default Address Handling**: If the deleted address was designated as the default shipping address, the customer must select a different address to become the new default before the deletion can proceed. This ensures the customer always has a default address for checkout convenience.

**Order History Preservation**: Deleting an address does not affect any existing orders. Orders preserve a complete snapshot of the address at the time of purchase for record-keeping and legal purposes. Historical orders will continue to display the address information as it existed when the order was placed.

**Authorization**: Only the customer who owns the address can delete it. Sellers and administrators cannot delete customer addresses.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implement the following business logic:

1. **Authentication Check**: Verify the customer is authenticated.

2. **Ownership Verification**: Query the address record and verify that address.customerId matches the authenticated customer's ID.
   - If no address exists with the given addressId OR the address belongs to a different customer: Return 404 Not Found (do not reveal whether the address exists to prevent enumeration attacks).
   - Log the unauthorized access attempt for security review.

3. **Default Address Check**: Check if the address is designated as the customer's default shipping address.
   - If it is the default address:
     - Option A: Automatically clear the default designation and proceed with deletion.
     - Option B: Check if the customer has other addresses. If yes, the system may require designation of a new default before deletion (implementation-dependent).
     - If it's the only address and designated as default with pending orders requiring shipping address, reject the deletion (per section 562).

4. **Delete Address**: Execute a hard delete on the address record. Addresses are permanently deleted (not soft-deleted).

5. **Return**: Return 204 No Content on successful deletion.

**Database Operations**:
- SELECT address by addressId to verify ownership
- DELETE address record

**Error Cases**:
- 404 Not Found: Address doesn't exist or belongs to different customer
- 403 Forbidden: Customer not authenticated
- 409 Conflict: Cannot delete the only default address when pending orders exist (if implementing strict default address requirement)

Include related user information (email, name) from parent tables for summary display. Exclude sensitive token values from response - only return metadata.

This endpoint serves dual purposes. Administrators can search through all registrations to identify pending approvals requiring review. Sellers can view their own registration history, tracking transitions from initial submission through approval or rejection states.

The search functionality supports sophisticated filtering by registration status (pending, approved, rejected), submission date ranges, and reviewer assignments. Pagination ensures efficient handling of potentially large registration datasets.

Access control is enforced through underlying permission layers:
- Administrators can view all registrations
- Sellers can only access their own registration records

Response includes summary information optimized for list displays, with efficient truncation of potentially nested historical data.

Query the ecommerce_mall_seller_registrations table with advanced filtering capabilities. Implement robust permission checks to restrict results based on the requesting actor's role:
- Administrators receive a comprehensive view of all registration records
- Sellers are limited to their own registration history entries

Support sophisticated filtering mechanisms:
- Status filtering: capture pending, approved, and rejected registrations
- Temporal filtering: query by submission date, review date, or modification timestamps
- Search by seller identifier or reviewer identifier

Implement pagination using cursor-based strategies to handle large dataset volumes efficiently. Default result limit is 20 registrations per request, with flexible page size configuration available.

Include computed fields for enhanced usability:
- Calculated registration duration
- Associated seller profile metadata

operations.description:
Reset a user account password using a valid password reset token.

This operation allows customers, sellers, and administrators to complete the password reset process by providing their unique reset token and new password. The system validates the token against all three user type tables (customers, sellers, administrators), verifies the token has not expired, and updates the user's password hash.

Upon successful password reset, the token is permanently deleted to prevent reuse, and all existing sessions for that user are invalidated for security. The user must log in again with their new password.

The new password must meet platform security requirements including minimum length and complexity. If the token is invalid, expired, or the new password fails validation, the operation is rejected with an appropriate error.
operations.name: resetPassword
operations.specification:
Implement password reset using token validation:

1. Search for the provided token in all three password reset tables:
   - ecommerce_mall_customer_password_resets (token unique constraint)
   - ecommerce_mall_seller_password_resets (token unique constraint) 
   - ecommerce_mall_admin_password_resets (token unique constraint)

2. Verify the token exists and has not expired (compare expires_at/created_at with current time).

3. Retrieve the associated user from the corresponding actor table:
   - customers table for customer tokens
   - sellers table for seller tokens
   - admins table for admin tokens

4. Validate the new password meets platform security requirements (minimum length, complexity rules).

5. Hash the new password using the platform's password hashing algorithm.

6. Update the user's password hash in their respective table within a transaction.

7. Delete the used password reset token record to prevent replay attacks.

8. Invalidate all existing sessions for this user by deleting session records from:
   - ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions
   - ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions
   - ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions

9. Handle edge cases:
   - Return 404 error if token not found in any table
   - Return 410 error if token has expired
   - Return 422 error if new password fails validation

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of audit log entries from the platform's governance audit trail.

This operation provides comprehensive access to the audit logs that record all significant administrative actions performed on the platform. The audit trail captures who performed an action, what action was taken, which resource was affected, and contextual metadata including IP address, user agent, and timestamp.

The platform maintains two types of audit records:
1. Administrator audit logs - tracking seller approvals, category management, product oversight, order management, and user ban/unban actions by regular administrators
2. Super administrator audit logs - tracking critical security events including administrator promotions/demotions, system-level configuration changes, and force actions

This endpoint supports advanced filtering by administrator, action type, resource type, resource ID, date ranges, and IP address. Results are sorted chronologically with newest entries first, supporting cursor-based pagination for efficient handling of large audit datasets.

Only administrators (admin and superAdmin roles) can access audit logs. Super administrators can view all audit records including those from other super administrators. Regular administrators have access to administrator audit logs but cannot access super administrator audit logs unless specifically authorized.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query both ecommerce_mall_admin_audit_logs and ecommerce_mall_super_admin_audit_logs tables based on the requester's privilege level.

For superAdmin requesters:
- Query both tables and aggregate results
- Include all fields: id, adminId/superAdminId, action/actionType, resourceType/targetType, resourceId/targetId, details/description, ip/ipAddress, userAgent, createdAt

For regular admin requesters:
- Query only ecommerce_mall_admin_audit_logs
- Restrict to records where admin_id matches requesting admin OR where resource involves accessible entities

Implementation logic:
1. Validate requester is authenticated as admin or superAdmin
2. Build WHERE conditions based on request body filters:
   - adminId: filter by specific administrator
   - actionTypes: array of action type strings (partial match supported)
   - resourceTypes: array of resource type strings
   - resourceId: exact resource ID match
   - dateFrom/dateTo: created_at timestamp range
   - ipAddress: exact or partial IP match
3. Apply sorting by created_at DESC (newest first)
4. Apply cursor-based pagination using created_at + id
5. Return paginated response with IEcommerceMallAuditLog.ISummary items

Edge cases:
- Empty result set when no logs match criteria
- Date range validation (dateFrom must be before dateTo)
- IP address format validation
- Action type case-insensitive matching

Error handling:
- Return 401/403 if requester lacks admin privileges
- Return 400 for invalid date formats or ranges
- Return 400 for malformed resource IDs

responseBody.description: Paginated list of audit log summaries matching the search criteria

operations.description:
Submit a request to become an administrator.

This operation allows registered customers and sellers to request elevation to administrator status. The request must include a reason explaining the user's qualifications, relevant experience, or motivation for seeking administrative privileges.

Upon successful submission, the request is created with 'pending' status and awaits review by a super administrator. Each user may only have one pending promotion request at any given time; attempting to submit a new request while one is already pending will result in a rejection.

The request is associated with the authenticated user (customer or seller) through polymorphic subtype relationships. Only users without current administrator status may submit promotion requests.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implementation requirements:

1. **Authentication**: Verify the user is authenticated as either a customer or seller.

2. **Authorization Check**: 
   - Verify the user does not already have administrator status
   - Query existing promotion requests for this user
   - Reject if any request with 'pending' status exists for this user (error: "You already have a pending promotion request")

3. **Request Validation**:
   - Validate reason field is provided and non-empty
   - Reason should have minimum length (e.g., 10 characters) and maximum length (e.g., 1000 characters)

4. **Database Transaction**:
   - Create record in ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_requests with:
     - id: generated UUID
     - status: 'pending'
     - reason: from request body
     - reviewer_id: null
     - rejection_reason: null
     - created_at: current timestamp
     - updated_at: current timestamp
   - Create corresponding subtype record based on user type:
     - If customer: insert into ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_customers
     - If seller: insert into ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_sellers
   - Both inserts must be in the same transaction

5. **Response**:
   - Return the created promotion request entity including:
     - id, status, reason, created_at, updated_at
     - Include requester information (customer or seller details)

6. **Error Handling**:
   - 401: User not authenticated
   - 403: User already has administrator status
   - 409: User already has a pending promotion request
   - 400: Missing or invalid reason field

7. **Side Effects**:
   - No snapshots created on initial submission (snapshots are created on status changes)
   - No notifications sent (administrators query pending requests)

responseBody.description: The newly created administrator promotion request with pending status

requestBody.description: Promotion request creation data including the reason for seeking administrator privileges

operations.description:
Approve or reject an administrator promotion request.

This operation allows super administrators to review pending promotion requests submitted by customers or sellers seeking administrative privileges. The super administrator can either approve the request, granting the requester regular administrator status, or reject the request with a reason.

When approved, the requester's status changes to approved and they gain administrator privileges. When rejected, the rejection_reason field captures the explanation for the denial, allowing the requester to understand why their request was not accepted and potentially submit a new request in the future.

The operation automatically sets the reviewer to the current authenticated super administrator and updates the review timestamp. A snapshot of the request state is created for audit trail purposes. Only requests with pending status can be reviewed; attempts to update already approved or rejected requests will fail.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Validate that the requesting user is a super administrator. Verify the promotion request exists and has pending status - reject if already approved or rejected.

If status is being changed to 'approved':
- Validate no rejection_reason is provided (cannot reject and approve simultaneously)
- Set reviewer_id to current super admin's ID
- Create corresponding Administrator record for the requester with grade 'regular'
- Create AdminPromotionRequestSnapshot for audit trail

If status is being changed to 'rejected':
- Validate rejection_reason is provided and non-empty
- Set reviewer_id to current super admin's ID
- Create AdminPromotionRequestSnapshot for audit trail

Update the updated_at timestamp. Return the full promotion request entity including the reviewer relationship.

Permanently deletes (cancels) a pending administrator promotion request from the system.

This operation allows super administrators to remove promotion requests that are no longer relevant or were submitted in error. Only requests with 'pending' status can be deleted; approved or rejected requests are preserved for audit purposes.

When a pending request is deleted:
- The request is soft-deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp
- The requester (customer or seller) can submit a new promotion request if desired
- No notification is sent to the requester (silent removal)

Approved requests cannot be deleted as the user has already been promoted to administrator status. Rejected requests cannot be deleted as they serve as historical records of the decision with the rejection reason preserved.

operations.specification:
Validate the request exists and is in 'pending' status. Reject with appropriate error if the request is already approved or rejected.

Perform soft delete by setting deleted_at to current timestamp. Do not hard delete the record to preserve data integrity and allow potential audit queries.

No associated snapshots are created for delete operations as this is a cancellation rather than a state change. The request simply transitions to a deleted state.

Authorization: Only super_admin role can access this endpoint. Regular administrators cannot delete promotion requests.

- The requester (customer or seller) can submit a new promotion request if desired

Approved requests cannot be deleted as the user has already been promoted to administrator status. Rejected requests cannot be deleted as they serve as historical records of the decision with the rejection reason preserved.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Validate the request exists and is in 'pending' status. Reject with appropriate error if the request is already approved or rejected.

Perform soft delete by setting deleted_at to current timestamp. Do not hard delete the record to preserve data integrity and allow potential audit queries.

No associated snapshots are created for delete operations as this is a cancellation rather than a state change. The request simply transitions to a deleted state.

Authorization: Only super_admin role can access this endpoint. Regular administrators cannot delete promotion requests.

This POST operation creates the request in 'pending' status, which is the required state for the DELETE operation to succeed. Only requests created through this endpoint can be subsequently deleted by super administrators.

operations.description:
Soft-deletes (cancels) a pending administrator promotion request from the system.

This operation allows super administrators to remove promotion requests that are no longer relevant or were submitted in error. Only requests with 'pending' status can be deleted; approved or rejected requests are preserved for audit purposes.

When a pending request is deleted:
- The request is soft-deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp
- The request is hidden from active queries but retained in the database for audit purposes
- The requester (customer or seller) can submit a new promotion request if desired
- No notification is sent to the requester (silent removal)

Approved requests cannot be deleted as the user has already been promoted to administrator status. Rejected requests cannot be deleted as they serve as historical records of the decision with the rejection reason preserved.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of snapshots for a specific admin promotion request.

Snapshots capture the complete state history of promotion request transitions. Each snapshot records the before and after states when a request's status changes (e.g., from pending to approved or rejected), including reviewer identities, status values, and associated reasons.

This operation provides audit trail visibility for:
- Super administrators reviewing promotion request history
- Compliance and security auditing
- Dispute resolution about promotion decisions

Snapshots are immutable records that preserve the exact state at each transition point. All fields including previous_review_id, new_reviewer_id, previous_status, new_status, previous_reason, and new_reason are captured for complete traceability.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_snapshots table filtering by admin_promotion_request_id matching the path parameter.
Support pagination with cursor-based or offset pagination.
Default sort order is created_at DESC (newest snapshots first).
Apply optional filters on:
- created_at date range
- previous_status / new_status
- previous_reviewer_id / new_reviewer_id
Join with ecommerce_mall_admins to get reviewer names for display (previousReviewer, newReviewer relations).
Return snapshot summaries including:
- id, created_at
- previous/new status transition
- previous/new reviewer info (id, name if denormalized)
- previous/new reasons
Exclude soft-deleted parent request snapshots only if parent is soft-deleted (though snapshots themselves are never deleted per immutability rules).
Return 404 if the promotion request does not exist or user lacks access.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of promotion request snapshots ordered by creation time (newest first)

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific immutable snapshot of an administrator promotion request state change.

This operation provides access to point-in-time records of promotion request modifications. Snapshots capture the complete state transition when a promotion request is approved or rejected, preserving both the previous and new values for compliance and dispute resolution.

The response includes reviewer identities (before and after), status values, rejection/approval reasons, and the exact timestamp of the state change. Administrators and the original requester can view snapshots for transparency in the promotion process.

Snapshots are immutable records that cannot be modified or deleted, ensuring a complete audit trail for all administrative privilege changes on the platform.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_snapshots table using both admin_promotion_request_id and id fields for precise record retrieval.

Join with ecommerce_mall_admins table to resolve previous_reviewer_id and new_reviewer_id to administrator details for the response.

Verify access permissions: the requesting user must be either (1) the original promotion requester, (2) an administrator, or (3) a super administrator. Unauthorized access attempts must be rejected.

Return the complete snapshot record including all captured state fields: previous status, new status, previous reason, new reason, reviewer identities, and creation timestamp.

Handle edge cases: return 404 if either the promotion request or snapshot does not exist; return 403 if the user lacks viewing permissions for this snapshot.

responseBody.description: Complete admin promotion request snapshot with reviewer details and state transition information
