operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of product categories.

This operation provides browsing capabilities for the platform's category hierarchy. Categories support a maximum nesting depth of two levels: parent categories (top-level) and subcategories (one level below). Each category has a unique name within its parent scope and optional description.

The response includes category summaries optimized for list displays, showing essential information such as name, description, and parent relationship. Pagination follows standard page-based navigation with a default page size of 20 items.

Soft-deleted categories are automatically excluded from results. When a category is deleted by an administrator, it becomes unavailable for browsing but its history is preserved for existing orders and audit purposes.

When filtering by parentId, the operation returns subcategories belonging to that specific parent category. When parentId is omitted or null, the operation returns top-level parent categories.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_categories table with pagination support.

Apply optional filters:
- parentId: Filter by parent category to get subcategories. When null or omitted, return top-level categories (where parent_id IS NULL).

Implement cursor-based pagination using createdAt and id as cursor fields for stable ordering.

Return paginated response with:
- data: Array of category summaries
- pagination: Cursor information for next/previous pages

Categories should be ordered by:
1. Parent categories first (null parent_id), then subcategories
2. Within same level, order by createdAt descending (newest first)

Include in summary:
- id, name, description
- parentId (null for top-level categories)
- createdAt, updatedAt
- subcategoryCount (if parent category, count of its subcategories)

Authorization: All authenticated users (customer, seller, admin, superAdmin) can access.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of category summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for category listing

prerequisites.description: Category entities must exist in the system before they can be searched and filtered. The admin category creation operation establishes the category records that will be returned by the search operation.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single category by its unique identifier.

This operation returns complete category information including its name, description, and hierarchical relationships. If the category is a subcategory, its parent category details are included. If the category has subcategories, those are listed as well.

This endpoint supports the category browsing experience for customers navigating the product catalog hierarchy. Categories are organized in a two-level hierarchy: parent categories at the top level and subcategories nested beneath them.

Categories implement soft delete—deleted categories cannot be retrieved through this endpoint. If a category with no products is deleted, it becomes unavailable for browsing. Products in deleted categories become uncategorized but remain accessible through other means.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_categories table by id (UUID primary key).

Exclude categories where deleted_at is not null (soft deleted categories).

Join with parent category via parent_id relationship if parent_id is set.

Join with subcategories to retrieve child categories where their parent_id equals this category's id (excluding soft deleted subcategories).

Return 404 if category not found or has been soft deleted.

Include all scalar fields: id, name, description, parent_id, created_at, updated_at.

Include parent object with id, name if parent exists.

Include subcategories array with id, name for each active subcategory ordered by name ASC.

responseBody.description: Complete category details including hierarchical relationships

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the category (UUID format)
parameters.name: categoryId

prerequisites.description: Category must be created before it can be retrieved by ID. The POST operation creates the category resource that the GET operation reads.

operations.description:
Create a new product category to organize products in the e-commerce platform.

This endpoint allows administrators to create categories that help customers discover products through hierarchical browsing. Categories support one level of nesting, meaning they can be either top-level categories (no parent) or subcategories of an existing parent category.

Each category requires a unique name within its parent scope. Name uniqueness comparisons are performed case-insensitively - names that differ only by case (e.g., 'Electronics' and 'electronics') are considered duplicates and will be rejected.

This operation is restricted to administrator users only. Customers and sellers cannot create categories.

When creating a subcategory (by providing parentId), the parent category must exist and not be deleted. The two-level hierarchy (parent + children) constraint prevents deeper nesting.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Validate the requesting user has administrator role. Validate the request body contains a non-empty name field and optional description and parentId fields.

If parentId is provided:
- Verify the parent category exists and is not deleted (deleted_at is null)
- The parent must be a top-level category (parent_id is null) to maintain the two-level hierarchy constraint

Check for duplicate category name using case-insensitive comparison within the same parent scope:
- If parentId is provided: check uniqueness within that parent_id
- If parentId is null (top-level): check uniqueness where parent_id is null
- If a category with the same name (case-insensitive) already exists in the same scope, reject with conflict error

Create a new category record in ecommerce_mall_categories table:
- Generate a new UUID for id
- Set parent_id from request (null for top-level)
- Set name as provided (preserve original case from input)
- Set description if provided, otherwise null
- Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp
- Set deleted_at to null

Insert the record and return the complete category entity including generated id and timestamps.

Error scenarios:
- 401 Unauthorized: User is not authenticated
- 403 Forbidden: User is not an administrator
- 400 Bad Request: Missing or invalid name, parent category does not exist, or parent is already a subcategory (would exceed 2-level depth)
- 409 Conflict: Category with the same name already exists within the same parent scope (case-insensitive)

responseBody.description: The newly created category with generated id, timestamps, and provided fields

requestBody.description: Category creation data including name, optional description, and optional parent category

operations.description:
Update an existing product category's information.

This operation allows administrators to modify category details including the name and description. Category names must be unique within the same parent category to prevent confusion in product organization. Top-level categories have globally unique names, while subcategories under different parents can share names.

Only administrators can update categories. Sellers and customers do not have permission to modify the category structure. This centralized management ensures a consistent and uniform taxonomy across the platform.

The category's hierarchical position (parent/child relationship) cannot be changed after creation through this operation. To reorganize categories, administrators must delete and recreate them with the desired structure.

Duplicate category names within the same parent scope are rejected with validation errors. The system performs case-insensitive uniqueness checks.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Validate the administrator's authorization to modify categories. Check that categoryId exists in ecommerce_mall_categories table.

Validate IUpdate request body fields:
- name: required, non-empty string, unique across all categories (case-insensitive check)
- description: optional string for category explanation

Perform unique name constraint check excluding the current category being updated. If another category already uses the requested name (case-insensitive), reject with validation error.

Update the category record with provided values. Preserve existing fields not included in the update.

Return the complete updated category entity including its id, name, description, parentId (if subcategory), and timestamps.

responseBody.description: The fully updated category entity with all fields

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the category to update
parameters.name: categoryId

requestBody.description: Category update data with name and optional description

prerequisites.description: Category must be created before it can be updated via PUT operation

operations.description:
Permanently removes a category from the platform.

When a category is deleted, any products previously assigned to that category become uncategorized. Uncategorized products remain on the platform and can still be found through search and direct links, but they do not appear when customers browse by category.

If a parent category with subcategories is deleted, all its subcategories are also deleted. Products in those deleted subcategories become uncategorized as well.

Category deletion requires administrator privileges and cannot be performed by sellers or customers. Deleted categories cannot be recovered.

This operation performs a soft delete, preserving the category record for audit purposes while marking it as inactive.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the caller has administrator privileges.

2. Find the category by categoryId from the ecommerce_mall_categories table.

3. If category not found or already deleted (deleted_at is not null), return 404 Not Found.

4. Check if the category has subcategories by querying ecommerce_mall_categories where parent_id = categoryId.

5. Begin a transaction:
   - Set deleted_at = current timestamp for the target category
   - For all subcategories (if any), set deleted_at = current timestamp
   - The database schema defines onDelete: Cascade for the parent relation, but we should explicitly handle subcategory deletion

6. Update all products in ecommerce_mall_products that reference this category or its subcategories to have category_id = null (uncategorized).

7. Commit the transaction.

8. Return 204 No Content with empty response body.

Edge cases:
- If category has active products, they become uncategorized (not deleted)
- Cascade deletion of subcategories happens automatically due to database constraints
- Soft delete preserves the category for historical reference in order snapshots

parameters.description: The UUID that uniquely identifies the category to delete
parameters.name: categoryId

prerequisites.description: A category must be created first before it can be deleted. The POST /ecommerceMall/admin/categories operation creates the category resource that provides the categoryId referenced in the DELETE operation path.

operations.description:
Search and retrieve a paginated list of products with optional filtering and sorting.

This endpoint allows customers to discover products through various search criteria including text search by product name, category filtering, price range filtering, and stock availability filtering. Results can be sorted by newest first, price ascending, or price descending.

The response includes product summaries optimized for browsing displays, containing the main thumbnail image, product name, pricing information, seller shop name, and average customer rating. Products without any variants are included in results but marked as unavailable for purchase.

Only active (non-deleted) products from approved sellers are returned in search results. The search uses GIN trigram indexing for efficient text matching on product names.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_products table filtering by deleted_at IS NULL to exclude soft-deleted products.

Join with ecommerce_mall_sellers to filter for approved sellers only (approval_status = 'approved' AND deleted_at IS NULL).

Apply search filters from request body:
- search: Use trigram similarity search on name field (GIN index) when provided
- categoryId: Filter by exact category_id match
- subcategoryId: Filter by category_id when subcategory is specified
- priceMin/priceMax: Filter by base_price range
- inStockOnly: When true, join with ecommerce_mall_product_variants and aggregate inventory from ecommerce_mall_inventory_records to filter products having at least one variant with quantity > 0

Apply sorting based on sortBy field:
- 'newest': ORDER BY created_at DESC
- 'priceAsc': ORDER BY base_price ASC
- 'priceDesc': ORDER BY base_price DESC

For each product in results, calculate:
- priceRange: MIN/MAX of variant prices (or base_price if no variant override)
- averageRating: AVG of ratings from ecommerce_mall_reviews where deleted_at IS NULL
- reviewCount: COUNT of non-deleted reviews
- thumbnailImage: image_url from first image (display_order = 0) via ecommerce_mall_product_images
- sellerShopName: from related ecommerce_mall_sellers profile

Implement cursor-based pagination for consistent performance with large datasets.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product summaries with thumbnail, pricing, seller info, and ratings

requestBody.description: Product search criteria including text search, filters, sorting, and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a single product by its unique identifier.

 This operation returns the complete product information including the product name, description, category assignment, and base price. The response includes all associated product variants (SKUs) with their option values, individual prices, and current stock quantities.

 Product images are returned in their display order, with the first image serving as the main thumbnail. Seller information including the shop name and description is included to help customers identify the product source.

 Customer reviews and ratings for the product are also included, showing the average rating and individual review details. This comprehensive data enables the product detail page to display all necessary information for customer purchase decisions.

 This endpoint is accessible to all authenticated users. Customers can view any active product. Sellers can view their own products including hidden or suspended ones. Administrators can view all products regardless of status for oversight purposes.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_products table by the provided productId UUID parameter. Join with ecommerce_mall_product_variants to fetch all variants including their SKU codes, option values, prices, and calculated stock quantities from inventory records. Join with ecommerce_mall_product_images to retrieve all associated images ordered by display_order. Join with ecommerce_mall_sellers and ecommerce_mall_seller_profiles to get seller shop information. Join with ecommerce_mall_reviews and ecommerce_mall_customers to get review data including ratings and reviewer names. Join with ecommerce_mall_categories to get category name and hierarchy information.

 Implement authorization checks: allow customers to access active products only (products with at least one variant), allow sellers to access their own products regardless of status, allow administrators to access any product. Return 404 if product not found or user lacks permission. Calculate average rating from non-deleted reviews. Calculate stock quantity by summing all inventory records for each variant.

responseBody.description: Complete product details including variants, images, seller information, and reviews

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product to retrieve (global scope)
parameters.name: productId

prerequisites.description: Product must be created by a seller before it can be retrieved. The productId path parameter references an existing Product record that must exist in the ecommerce_mall_products table.

operations.description:
Create a new product listing on the platform.

This endpoint allows sellers to register new products for customer purchase. A product requires a name, description, category selection, and base price. The product is exclusively associated with the authenticated seller who creates it.

Only sellers with approved registration status can create products. Pending or rejected sellers are blocked from this operation until their registration is approved.

Upon successful creation, the product enters an active state. The product becomes visible in search results and category listings once it has at least one variant added. Every product edit (including creation) creates a snapshot preserving the product state.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the authenticated user is a seller with approved registration status. If status is pending or rejected, return 403 Forbidden.

2. Validate request body fields:
   - name: required, non-empty string, max length per business rules
   - description: required, non-empty string
   - categoryId: required, valid UUID referencing existing category
   - basePrice: required, positive number

3. Verify the category exists in the database. If not found, return 404 Not Found.

4. Create the product record with:
   - Generated UUID as primary key
   - name, description, basePrice from request
   - categoryId referencing the selected category
   - sellerId set to the authenticated seller's ID
   - createdAt timestamp set to current time

5. Return the created product entity with all fields populated.

responseBody.description: The newly created product with all fields populated

requestBody.description: Product creation data including name, description, category ID, and base price

prerequisites.description: Product category must exist before a product can be assigned to it. The category_id request body field in product creation references an existing category resource.

operations.description:
Updates an existing product's details.

This operation allows sellers to modify their product information including name, description, category assignment, and base price. Only the product owner (the seller who created it) can perform updates.

Per the Snapshot Principle, every successful update automatically creates a product snapshot that preserves the previous state of the product and all its variants. This snapshot includes all product fields (name, description, category, base price, images) and variant states at that moment, enabling dispute resolution and audit trails.

The operation validates seller ownership before allowing any modifications. Attempts to update a product owned by another seller will be rejected. Soft-deleted products cannot be updated until restored.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId} to retrieve current state, POST /products to create new products.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Implement the following:

1. **Authentication & Authorization**: Verify the requesting user is an authenticated seller. Check that the product belongs to the requesting seller by comparing seller_id. Return 403 Forbidden if ownership mismatch.

2. **Existence Check**: Verify the product exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null). Return 404 Not Found if product doesn't exist or is deleted.

3. **Snapshot Creation**: Before applying updates, create a product snapshot record capturing the current state:
   - Copy all current product fields (name, description, category_id, base_price)
   - Create product snapshot image records for all current images
   - Create product variant snapshots for all variants of this product
   - Link the snapshot to the product for audit trail

4. **Field Updates**: Apply the provided fields from the request body:
   - name: Product display name (required in request)
   - description: Detailed product description (required in request)  
   - categoryId: Category assignment (required, must reference existing category)
   - basePrice: Base price value (required, must be positive number)

5. **Validation**: Validate all fields per business rules:
   - Name and description must be non-empty strings
   - Category must exist and not be soft-deleted
   - Base price must be a positive number

6. **Update Execution**: Update the product record in ecommerce_mall_products table, set updated_at to current timestamp.

7. **Response**: Return the full updated product entity including all fields (id, sellerId, categoryId, name, description, basePrice, createdAt, updatedAt).

Edge Cases:
- If seller registration is pending/rejected, block the operation (per Pre-Approval Operation Blocking rule)
- If category is changed, the product moves to the new category automatically
- Concurrent modifications: Use optimistic locking via updated_at timestamp to detect conflicts

responseBody.description: The updated product with all fields

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the product to update
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: Product update fields

prerequisites.description: The product must exist before its attributes can be updated. This POST operation creates the product entity that provides the productId used in the update path.

operations.description:
Soft-deletes a product and removes it from active listings.

This operation allows sellers to delete their own products when they are no longer needed or available. The product is soft-deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp, which removes it from search results and category listings while preserving the record for historical order reference and dispute resolution.

Before deletion, the system validates that there are no pending order items with 'paid' or 'shipped' status for any variant of the product, and no pending cancellation or refund requests.

Upon successful deletion:
- The product is soft-deleted and no longer appears in search results or category listings
- All product variants are cascade deleted
- All inventory records for those variants are removed
- All product images are removed from active listings
- Product snapshots are preserved for purchase history and dispute resolution

The operation returns the deleted product details for client state management.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Authorization: Verify the authenticated user is a seller who owns the product (seller_id matches authenticated seller).

2. Blocker Validation: Query order_items table joined with product_variants to check for any order items with status 'paid' OR 'shipped' belonging to any variant of the product. If any found, return 409 Conflict with error message indicating pending orders exist.

3. Service Request Validation: Query cancellation_requests and refund_requests tables joined with order_items and product_variants to check for any pending (unresponded) requests. If found, return 409 Conflict.

4. Soft Delete Execution: Set deleted_at timestamp to current time on ecommerce_mall_products record with productId. The schema defines onDelete: Cascade for related records, which will handle variants, images, and inventory records.

5. Return the deleted product entity including its soft-deleted state.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product to delete (global scope, UUID format)
parameters.name: productId

prerequisites.description: Product must be created before it can be deleted. The productId path parameter in the DELETE operation references the identifier returned from this creation operation.

operations.description:
Reorder the images associated with a product.

This operation allows sellers to change the display sequence of product images, including which image appears first as the main thumbnail. Images are displayed to customers in the order defined by the seller.

When images are reordered, the new first image automatically becomes the main thumbnail that appears in search results and category listings. Sort orders must remain sequential without gaps, and each image must have a unique sort order within the product.

Image changes trigger product snapshot creation to preserve the visual state history for dispute resolution and audit purposes. Snapshots capture the complete set of images, their order, and which image was designated as the main thumbnail at that moment.

Only sellers who own the product can reorder its images. The system validates that the requesting seller has ownership rights before applying any changes.
operations.name: updateOrder
operations.specification:
Validate that the requesting seller owns the product identified by productId. Query all non-deleted images for the product from ecommerce_mall_product_images table ordered by display_order.

Validate the reorder request: ensure all image IDs in the request belong to this product, ensure no duplicate image IDs, ensure all existing images are included (unless specified otherwise by requirements).

Update display_order values for each image according to the new sequence provided in the request. The first position (lowest display_order) becomes the main thumbnail.

Create a product snapshot to record the image state change for audit trail. The snapshot preserves the complete set of images and their ordering at this moment.

Return the updated list of images with their new display_order values and image URLs.

responseBody.description: List of product images with updated display order

parameters.description: UUID of the product whose images are being reordered
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: New ordering configuration for product images

prerequisites.description: Product must exist before images can be associated with it and reordered. The productId path parameter references the product entity.
Images must be uploaded to the product before they can be reordered. The reordering operation updates display_order of existing image records.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific product image by its unique identifier.

This endpoint returns the complete details of a single product image associated with a product. The image includes its URL, display order within the product's image collection, and creation timestamps.

The first image in the display order (order 0) serves as the main thumbnail for the product in search results and category listings.

Authentication is required to access product images. Sellers can view images for products they own. Administrators can view images for any product.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Validate both productId and productImageId are valid UUIDs.

Query the ecommerce_mall_product_images table:
- Join with ecommerce_mall_products to verify product exists and ownership
- Filter by: id = productImageId AND product_id = productId
- Include soft deleted images (they should still be retrievable)

Return 404 if image not found.
Return 403 if caller is a seller and does not own the product.

The image_url field contains a URI string referencing the stored image file.
The display_order field indicates the image's position in the product's gallery, with 0 being the main thumbnail.

created_at and updated_at timestamps use timestamptz format.

responseBody.description: Complete product image entity

parameters.description: Product unique identifier (UUID)
parameters.name: productId

parameters.description: Product image unique identifier (UUID)
parameters.name: productImageId

prerequisites.description: Product must exist before images can be associated with it. The product_id foreign key constraint requires a valid product record.
Product image must be uploaded before it can be retrieved. The productImageId path parameter references the image's primary key.

operations.description:
Upload a new image to a product.

Sellers can upload multiple images for each product they own. The uploaded image is associated with the specified product and becomes part of its visual presentation.

The first image uploaded for a product automatically becomes the main thumbnail image, which appears in search results and category listings. Subsequent images provide detailed views from different angles or show product features.

Images help customers evaluate products before making purchase decisions. High-quality visual presentation allows sellers to present their products professionally.

**Authorization**: Only the product owner (seller) can upload images. Cross-seller image management is blocked.

**Display Order**: The system automatically assigns the next available display order. The image at display order 0 serves as the main thumbnail.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Validate that the authenticated user is the owner of the product (seller ownership check).

Validate the request body:
- imageUrl: must be a valid URI string pointing to the uploaded image file

Determine the display order for the new image:
- Query existing images for the product where deleted_at is null
- If no images exist, assign display_order = 0 (becomes main thumbnail)
- If images exist, assign display_order = max(existing display_order) + 1

Insert a new record into ecommerce_mall_product_images with:
- id: generate new UUID
- product_id: from path parameter
- image_url: from request body
- display_order: calculated as above
- created_at: current timestamp
- updated_at: current timestamp
- deleted_at: null

Return the created image entity with all fields including the assigned display_order.

**Error Handling**:
- 404: Product not found or product is soft-deleted
- 403: Authenticated user is not the product owner
- 400: Invalid image URL format

responseBody.description: The created product image entity with assigned display order

operations.description:
Update a product image's display order to reorder images within a product.

This operation allows sellers to modify the sequence position of a specific product image. Changing the display order affects how images appear on the product detail page and determines which image serves as the main thumbnail (the image at display_order 1).

When an image's position is changed, the system automatically resequences other images to maintain gap-free ordering. All images within a product must have unique display orders starting from 1 without gaps.

Only the seller who owns the product can modify its images. Cross-seller image management is blocked per business rules. The operation updates the updated_at timestamp and returns the complete updated image record with its new display position.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
`Authenticate the requesting seller.

Validate product ownership:
- Load the product_image by productImageId from the URL path
- Join with parent product to verify product_id matches the path parameter
- Verify the product's seller_id matches the authenticated seller
- If ownership mismatch, return 403 Forbidden (cross-seller block)

Validate request body:
- display_order must be an integer >= 0
- display_order must be within valid range (0 to current image count - 1)

Execute reordering transaction:
- Begin database transaction
- If moving image to a lower position (earlier in sequence):
  - Increment display_order by 1 for all images with display_order >= new_position AND display_order < old_position
- If moving image to a higher position (later in sequence):
  - Decrement display_order by 1 for all images with display_order > old_position AND display_order <= new_position
- Update the target image's display_order to the new position
- Update the updated_at timestamp to now
- Commit transaction

Return the complete updated image entity including:
- id, product_id, image_url, display_order, created_at, updated_at

Edge cases to handle:
- Requesting same position (no-op, just update timestamp)
- Invalid display_order value (validation error)
- Image not found (404)
- Product not found or mismatch (404)
- Cross-seller access attempt (403)

responseBody.description: The updated product image with its new display order and timestamps

operations.description:

This operation allows sellers to delete images from their own products or administrators to delete images from any product. When an image is deleted, the remaining images' display order is automatically reorganized to maintain a continuous sequence without gaps. If the deleted image was positioned as the main thumbnail (display_order 0), the next image in the sequence automatically becomes the new thumbnail.

The deletion uses soft delete semantics where the image record is preserved with a deletion timestamp for audit purposes and snapshot integrity. The image will no longer appear in the product's active image gallery or on product detail pages.

Authorization requires either ownership of the product (for sellers) or administrator privileges. Unauthorized deletion attempts will be rejected.

Reassign display_order values sequentially starting from 0 to eliminate any gaps caused by the deletion. Update each remaining image's display_order and updated_at timestamp. Return the deleted image record with its state at the time of deletion.

operations.description:
Create a new product variant for a specific product.

This operation allows sellers to add SKU-level variants to their products. Each variant represents a distinct purchasable configuration defined by option combinations such as color and size. Every variant must have a unique SKU code within the product and can optionally specify a price override.

The variant becomes immediately available for inventory management and customer purchase once created. Option values (e.g., Color=Red, Size=Large) are specified in the request and stored in a normalized structure for efficient querying.

Authentication required: Seller only. The seller must own the product to create variants for it.
operations.name: create

1. Validate that the requesting seller owns the product identified by productId.
2. Validate that the SKU code is unique within the product (check against existing non-deleted variants).
3. Validate that all option names and values are non-empty strings.
4. Generate a new UUID for the variant id.
5. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp (UTC).
6. Set deleted_at to null (active variant).
7. Insert the variant record into ecommerce_mall_product_variants table.
8. For each option in the request, insert a record into ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options table with the variant id.
9. Return the complete variant entity including the nested options.

Edge cases:
- Duplicate SKU code within the same product: Return 409 Conflict.
- Product not found or not owned by seller: Return 404 Not Found.
- Empty option array: Allowed (variant with no options).
- Negative price: Return 400 Bad Request (price must be positive if provided).
- Soft-deleted variant with same SKU: Allow creation (treat as new variant).

operations.description:
Update an existing product variant's attributes.

This operation allows sellers to modify variant details including the SKU code, option values (such as color and size combinations), and variant-specific price. The variant must belong to the specified product.

Every successful update creates an immutable snapshot of the previous variant state, preserving the complete configuration for audit trails and dispute resolution. Snapshots record the SKU code, option values, and price at the time of modification.

**Authorization**: Only the seller who owns the parent product can update its variants.

**Validation Rules**:
- The SKU code must be unique across the entire platform
- Option values must be valid key-value pairs representing product configurations
- Price must be a positive number if provided
- The variant must belong to the specified product

**Related Operations**:
- `POST /products/{productId}/variants` - Create a new variant
- `DELETE /products/{productId}/variants/{productVariantId}` - Remove a variant
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Implement variant update with the following logic:

1. **Authorization Check**: Verify the requesting seller owns the product identified by productId. Return 403 Forbidden if not authorized.

2. **Existence Validation**: 
   - Verify the product exists and is not deleted
   - Verify the variant exists and belongs to the specified product
   - Return 404 Not Found if either doesn't exist

3. **SKU Uniqueness Check**: 
   - If the SKU code is being changed, verify no other variant (under any product) uses the same SKU code
   - Return 409 Conflict if SKU is already in use

4. **Snapshot Creation** (BEFORE applying changes):
   - Query current variant state (skuCode, option values, price)
   - Insert a new record into ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshots with:
     - variant_id = the variant's id
     - sku_code = current SKU
     - price = current price
     - created_at = current timestamp
   - Copy current option values to ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshot_option_values

5. **Apply Updates**:
   - Update the variant record with new values from request body
   - Update option values in ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options:
     - Delete existing option records for this variant
     - Insert new option records from the request

6. **Return Updated Variant**:
   - Fetch the complete updated variant with its option values
   - Include current stock quantity calculated from inventory records

**Database Transactions**:
- Wrap snapshot creation, variant update, and option updates in a single transaction to ensure atomicity

**Error Handling**:
- 400 Bad Request: Invalid option format, negative price, or missing required fields
- 403 Forbidden: Seller does not own the product
- 404 Not Found: Product or variant not found
- 409 Conflict: SKU code already in use by another variant

**Edge Cases**:
- If the variant is part of pending orders (paid or shipped status), the update is still allowed but sellers should be cautious as customers may have already purchased based on the old configuration
- Stock quantity is managed separately through inventory records and cannot be modified through this endpoint

responseBody.description: The updated product variant with complete details including option values and current stock quantity

operations.description:
Permanently removes a product variant from the seller's product catalog.

This operation deletes a specific variant by its unique identifier. The system validates that no blocking conditions exist before allowing deletion.

Deletion is blocked if:
- There are pending order items with 'paid' or 'shipped' status for this variant
- There are pending cancellation requests for this variant
- There are pending refund requests for this variant

When the last remaining variant of a product is deleted, the product is automatically marked as unavailable for purchase. Deleted variants no longer appear in customer-facing listings and cannot be added to shopping carts.

Inventory records associated with the deleted variant are preserved for historical tracking but excluded from current stock calculations. The variant is soft-deleted to maintain referential integrity with historical orders.

This operation can only be performed by the seller who owns the product.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implement the variant deletion with the following logic:

1. **Authorization**: Verify the requesting user is an authenticated seller and owns the product referenced by productId.

2. **Variant Existence Check**: Verify the productVariantId exists under the specified productId. Return 404 if not found or already deleted (deleted_at is not null).

3. **Pending Order Items Validation**: Query ecommerce_mall_order_items for records where variant_id matches productVariantId and status is 'paid' or 'shipped'. If any exist, reject with 409 CONFLICT and error code 'VARIANT_HAS_PENDING_ORDERS'.

4. **Pending Cancellation Requests Validation**: Query ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests joined with order_items where variant_id matches productVariantId and status is 'pending'. If any exist, reject with 409 CONFLICT and error code 'VARIANT_HAS_PENDING_CANCELLATIONS'.

5. **Pending Refund Requests Validation**: Query ecommerce_mall_refund_requests joined with order_items where variant_id matches productVariantId and status is 'pending'. If any exist, reject with 409 CONFLICT and error code 'VARIANT_HAS_PENDING_REFUNDS'.

6. **Soft Delete Execution**: Set the deleted_at field to current timestamp for the variant record.

7. **Last Variant Check**: Query if any other active variants (deleted_at is null) exist for the same product_id. If this was the last variant, mark the product as unavailable in the product record.

8. **Response**: Return the soft-deleted variant record including the updated deleted_at timestamp.

All validation checks must pass in a single transaction to ensure data consistency.

This operation returns the complete state of a product at a specific point in time. The snapshot includes all product fields (name, description, category reference, base price), associated images with their display order, and snapshots of all product variants existing at that moment.

Product snapshots are immutable records created automatically whenever a product is modified. They serve as historical evidence for audit trails and dispute resolution.

Access control: Only administrators can retrieve product snapshots. This endpoint provides comprehensive visibility into product history for policy enforcement and dispute resolution purposes. Snapshots remain accessible even after product deletion.

Related operations: List all snapshots for a product via the product snapshots index endpoint.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots table by snapshot_id and product_id.

Authorization checks:
1. Verify the requesting user is authenticated as either a seller or administrator
2. If seller: verify the product's seller_id matches the requesting seller's ID
3. If administrator: allow access to any product snapshot

Database query:
- Join with ecommerce_mall_product_snapshot_images to retrieve all associated images ordered by display_order
- Join with ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshots to retrieve all variant snapshots that existed at the time

Return the complete snapshot object including:
- Snapshot metadata (id, product_id, created_at)
- Product fields at snapshot time (category_id, name, description, base_price)
- Nested array of snapshot images (url, display_order)
- Nested array of variant snapshots (sku_code, price, option values)

Edge cases:
- Return 404 if snapshot doesn't exist or doesn't belong to the specified product
- Return 403 if seller attempts to access another seller's product snapshot

responseBody.description: Complete product snapshot including images and variant snapshots

operations.description:
Search and list images associated with a specific product snapshot.

This operation retrieves a paginated list of product snapshot images in their display order at the time the snapshot was captured. Images are returned with their display sequence and URL references, allowing complete reconstruction of the product's visual presentation state.

Each snapshot contains the complete set of images that existed at the moment of snapshot creation, including their sort order and which image served as the main thumbnail (display_order = 1). This preserves the exact visual presentation customers would have seen for dispute resolution and historical reference.

Only authorized parties (product owners and administrators) can view snapshot images.

Query ecommerce_mall_product_snapshot_images filtering by the provided snapshotId from path parameter.

Apply optional search filters from request body on display_order range (min/max) or specific display positions.
Support pagination with cursor or offset-based strategies as configured.
Sort results by display_order ascending to maintain the original visual presentation sequence.
Return paginated list with image URL, display_order, and created_at timestamp for each image.

Authorization: Verify caller has permission to view the parent product snapshot (product owner or admin).

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of immutable snapshots for a specific product variant.

This operation returns the complete history of changes made to a product variant over time. Each snapshot captures the variant's state at the moment of a modification, including the SKU code, price, and all option values. Snapshots are automatically created whenever a seller edits any variant attribute.

Snapshots serve as historical records for dispute resolution, audit compliance, and change tracking. The operation supports filtering by date range to view snapshots from a specific time period. Results are ordered by creation time (newest first) to present the change history in chronological order.

Access is restricted to the variant's owner (seller) and administrators. The immutable nature of snapshots is strictly enforced - no modifications can be made to historical records.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshots table filtered by product_variant_id matching the path parameter.

Validation rules:
1. Verify the variant exists via product_variant_id reference before querying snapshots
2. Authorization check: Only the product owner (seller) or administrators can view snapshots
3. Permission denial returns 403 Forbidden

Filtering capabilities:
- createdAtFrom: Filter snapshots created on or after this timestamp (ISO 8601)
- createdAtTo: Filter snapshots created on or before this timestamp (ISO 8601)
- Both filters can be combined for date range queries

Sorting: Descending order on created_at (newest snapshots first).

Pagination: Supports cursor-based or offset pagination with configurable page size.

Response structure:
- Total count of matching snapshots
- Snapshot data array with id, sku_code, price, created_at, and embedded option_values
- Option values are joined from ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshot_option_values child table

Edge cases:
- Variant with no edit history returns empty list with zero count
- Invalid date ranges (from > to) should return empty result or validation error
- Deleted variants remain accessible for snapshot viewing due to audit trail requirements

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product variant snapshots ordered by creation time (newest first)

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific product variant snapshot by its unique identifier.

Product variant snapshots are immutable point-in-time records that preserve the complete state of a variant at the moment of modification. Each snapshot captures the SKU code, price, and all option values that existed before a change was made.

Snapshots serve as the authoritative audit trail for dispute resolution and historical reference. They cannot be modified or deleted after creation and remain preserved even if the parent variant is later deleted.

Authorization rules:
- Sellers can view snapshots of their own product variants
- Administrators can view snapshots of any product variant on the platform

This operation returns the complete snapshot record including the captured SKU code, price at the time of snapshot, creation timestamp, and associated option value records stored in the normalized child table.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Implement authorization checking based on user role:

1. For seller role: Verify the product variant identified by variantId belongs to the authenticated seller by joining with ecommerce_mall_product_variants -> ecommerce_mall_products -> seller_id
2. For admin/superAdmin roles: Allow access to any snapshot

Query the ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshots table by snapshotId primary key.
Include related option values from ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshot_option_values child table joined by snapshot_id.

Handle error cases:
- If snapshot not found: return 404 error
- If variantId in path does not match the snapshot's product_variant_id: return 404 (prevent information leakage about snapshot existence under wrong variant)
- If seller attempts to access another seller's snapshot: return 403 Forbidden

Return the full snapshot entity with all fields: id, product_variant_id, sku_code, price, created_at, and nested array of option values.

operations.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of option values from a product variant snapshot.

Product variant snapshots capture the complete state of a product variant at a specific point in time, including all option values that define the variant's characteristics (such as color, size, material, or other distinguishing attributes). Option values are stored as key-value pairs within the snapshot to preserve the exact configuration that existed when the snapshot was created.

This operation supports searching and filtering through the option values within a specific snapshot. Results are returned in a paginated format. Snapshots are immutable and represent historical states; they cannot be modified or deleted.

The option values provide the exact attribute combinations that distinguished this variant from others of the same product at the time the snapshot was captured.

operations.description:
Retrieves a single option value record from a product variant snapshot.

This operation returns the stored option configuration for a specific variant at the point in time when the snapshot was created. Option values represent key-value pairs that define variant characteristics such as color, size, material, or other configurable attributes. For example, an option value might represent 'Color: Red' or 'Size: Large'.

Product variant snapshots are immutable records that preserve the exact state of a variant for audit trails and dispute resolution. This endpoint allows authorized users (sellers who own the product, administrators, and customers who have purchased the variant) to inspect historic option configurations. The snapshotId path parameter identifies which variant snapshot to query, and the optionValueId identifies the specific option-value pair within that snapshot.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Retrieve a single option value record from ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshot_option_values table.

Query Conditions:
- Verify the option value exists with the given optionValueId
- Verify the option value belongs to the snapshot identified by snapshotId (validate parent relationship)
- If either condition fails, return 404 NotFound
- If snapshotId does not match the option value's parent snapshot, return 404 (don't expose that it exists but belongs to different snapshot)

Authorization:
- Check the calling actor has permission to access the variant snapshot
- Sellers can access snapshots of their own products
- Customers can access snapshots for their purchased order items
- Administrators can access any snapshot

Response includes:
- id: UUID of the option value record
- ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshot_id: The parent snapshot ID
- option_name: The attribute name (e.g., 'Color', 'Size')
- option_value: The attribute value (e.g., 'Red', 'Large')
- created_at: Timestamp when this snapshot was created

operations.description:
Retrieve the product snapshot associated with a specific order item.

This operation returns an immutable record of the product state at the time of purchase, including the product name, description, category information, and base price as they appeared when the order was placed. Product snapshots are automatically created during order creation to ensure accurate historical records for dispute resolution, order history viewing, and legal compliance.

The snapshot preserves the complete product state including associated images, preventing changes to the original product from affecting historical order data. This allows customers to verify what they purchased, sellers to reference past product states, and administrators to resolve disputes based on the exact product information presented at the time of purchase.

Access to this endpoint requires proper authentication. Customers can only view snapshots for their own orders, while sellers can view snapshots for order items containing their products. Administrators have access to all order item snapshots for oversight and dispute resolution purposes.
operations.name: atProductSnapshot
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_order_item_product_snapshots table by order_item_id using the provided orderItemId path parameter. 

The query should:
1. Lookup the product snapshot record where order_item_id matches the provided orderItemId
2. Join with ecommerce_mall_order_item_product_snapshot_images to retrieve all associated image URLs with their sort order
3. Order images by sort_order ascending to maintain the correct presentation sequence
4. Include the related category information if the category still exists

Validation rules:
- Verify the requesting user has permission to access this order item (customer must own the order, or seller must be the product owner, or user must be an administrator)
- Return 404 if no snapshot exists for the given order item (should not happen in normal operation as snapshots are created during order creation)

The response should include all snapshot fields plus the array of images ordered by sort_order.

responseBody.description: The product snapshot record preserving product state at purchase time, including all images

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the order item whose product snapshot is being retrieved
parameters.name: orderItemId

operations.description:

This endpoint returns the immutable variant snapshot that was captured when the order was placed. The snapshot preserves the exact state of the product variant at the time of purchase, including the SKU code, option values (such as color and size), and the variant-specific price.

Variant snapshots are created automatically during order creation and remain unchanged throughout the order's lifecycle. The snapshot ensures that even if the seller later modifies or deletes the product variant, the customer's order history still accurately reflects the item they bought.

This endpoint is typically used when displaying order details to customers, sellers, or administrators who need to see the exact product configuration that was ordered.

operations.description:
Retrieves the details of a specific shopping cart item by its ID.

This endpoint returns complete information about a single cart item including the product details, selected variant options, quantity, and pricing. The cart item represents a customer's selection of a specific product variant with the intent to purchase.

**Authorization Required**: Customer must be authenticated and can only access cart items belonging to their own account. Attempts to access another customer's cart items will be rejected per access boundary enforcement rules.

**Related Operations**: 
- `PATCH /cart-items` - List/search cart items
- `POST /cart-items` - Add item to cart
- `PUT /cart-items/{cartItemId}` - Update cart item quantity
- `DELETE /cart-items/{cartItemId}` - Remove item from cart
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Implement cart item retrieval by ID with strict ownership verification:

1. **Authentication Check**: Verify the requesting customer is authenticated via JWT session.

2. **Ownership Verification**: 
   - Query the cart_items table for the record matching the provided cartItemId
   - Verify the cart item's customer_id matches the authenticated customer's ID
   - If ownership mismatch → return 403 Forbidden (per section [367] Cart Access Boundary Enforcement)

3. **Data Retrieval**:
   - Join with ecommerce_mall_product_variants to get variant details (SKU code, option values, price)
   - Join with ecommerce_mall_products to get product details (name, description, images)
   - Join with ecommerce_mall_sellers and ecommerce_mall_seller_profiles to get shop name
   - Calculate subtotal as quantity × variant price

4. **Response Construction**:
   - Return full cart item details including:
     - Cart item ID, customer ID, variant ID
     - Product name and main image
     - Variant option values (color, size, etc.)
     - Individual variant price
     - Quantity in cart
     - Subtotal calculation
     - Stock availability status (compare quantity against current inventory)

5. **Error Handling**:
   - 404 Not Found: Cart item with given ID does not exist
   - 403 Forbidden: Cart item exists but belongs to different customer (security boundary)
   - 401 Unauthorized: Missing or invalid authentication token

6. **Performance Considerations**:
   - Use indexed lookup on cart_items.id (primary key)
   - Eager load related entities to minimize database round-trips

operations.description:
Add a product variant to the authenticated customer's shopping cart.

This operation allows customers to add specific product variants (not just products) to their shopping cart for later purchase. Customers must specify the exact variant and the desired quantity.

When adding an item that already exists in the cart (same variant), the quantities are combined rather than creating a separate line item, as enforced by the unique constraint on customer-variant combinations.

The operation validates that the product variant exists, is not deleted, and has sufficient stock before adding to the cart. If stock is insufficient, the operation will still succeed but mark the item with a warning status.

Cart items persist across browsing sessions until the customer checks out, removes them, or the cart expires.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Verify customer authentication from session/jwt token
2. Validate the product_variant_id exists in ecommerce_mall_product_variants table
3. Check that the variant's deleted_at is NULL (variant is active)
4. Validate quantity > 0
5. Check for existing cart item with same customer_id and product_variant_id
   - If exists: UPDATE existing record, add new quantity to existing quantity
   - If not exists: INSERT new cart item record
6. Create cart item with customer_id (from auth), product_variant_id, and quantity
7. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp
8. Return the created/updated cart item with joined product and variant details

Edge cases:
- If variant doesn't exist: Return 404
- If variant is deleted (soft-deleted): Return 410 Gone
- If quantity <= 0: Return 400 Bad Request
- Stock availability is checked but doesn't block creation (warning attached to response)

operations.description:
Update the quantity of an existing cart item.

This operation allows authenticated customers to modify the quantity of a product variant already in their shopping cart. The cart item is identified by its unique ID, and only the quantity field can be updated — the product variant and customer association remain unchanged.

When the quantity is updated, the cart item's updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed. The new quantity can be any positive integer greater than zero. If a customer wants to remove an item entirely, they should use the delete endpoint instead of setting quantity to zero.

This operation enforces strict access control — customers can only update cart items belonging to their own account. Attempts to access or modify another customer's cart items will be rejected.

The response returns the complete updated cart item including its product variant details, allowing the client to refresh the cart display with the new quantity and recalculated subtotal.

operations.specification: Validate that the authenticated customer owns the cart item with the given cartItemId. If not owned by the customer, reject with forbidden error. Validate the request body contains a valid quantity (positive integer greater than zero). Update the cart item record in ecommerce_mall_cart_items table, setting the new quantity and updating the updated_at timestamp. Return the complete cart item entity with its associated product variant information for display purposes. Handle edge case where cart item has been soft-deleted (deleted_at is set) by treating it as not found.

operations.description:
Removes a cart item from the customer's shopping cart.

This operation marks the cart item as deleted by setting the soft delete timestamp. The cart item is removed from the customer's active cart and will no longer appear in cart listings.

Security: Customers can only delete cart items belonging to their own account. Attempts to delete another customer's cart items will be rejected with a 403 Forbidden error.

The cart item reference is validated before deletion to ensure it exists and belongs to the authenticated customer.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Soft delete the cart item by setting the deleted_at timestamp to current time.

Validation steps:
1. Verify the cart item exists by id (cartItemId parameter)
2. Verify the cart item's customer_id matches the authenticated customer's id
3. If either check fails, reject with appropriate error (404 for not found, 403 for ownership violation)

Database operation:
- Update ecommerce_mall_cart_items table
- Set deleted_at = NOW()
- WHERE id = cartItemId AND customer_id = currentUserId AND deleted_at IS NULL

Edge cases:
- Cart item already deleted: return 404 (item not found in active cart)
- Cart item belongs to different customer: return 403 (access denied)
- Invalid UUID format: return 400 (bad request)

The soft delete pattern preserves the record for potential audit or recovery purposes while removing it from active listings.

   - Seller information from ecommerce_mall_sellers

7. Return the full order item entity

Edge cases to handle:
- Soft-deleted order items should still be accessible to sellers and admins for historical records, but customers may receive a filtered view
- Include related shipment information if the item has been shipped

operations.description:
Confirm delivery receipt of a shipment by the customer.

This operation allows a customer to mark a shipment as manually delivered after receiving the physical package. When confirmed, the shipment status transitions from 'In Transit' to 'Delivered', and all order items contained within that shipment are automatically updated to 'delivered' status simultaneously.

The delivery confirmation is recorded in the shipment delivery tracking system with the customer's ID, timestamp, and manual confirmation flag. Once confirmed, the order items become eligible for refund requests according to the 7-day refund policy window.

This operation can only be performed by the order owner (customer) and only for shipments that have not yet been delivered. The shipment must be in 'In Transit' status for delivery confirmation to be valid.
operations.name: confirm
operations.specification:
Transaction Flow:

1. Authorization Check
   - Verify the requesting actor is a customer
   - Verify the shipment belongs to an order owned by this customer
   - Reject with 403 Forbidden if customer does not own the corresponding order

2. Shipment State Validation
   - Fetch shipment by shipmentId from ecommerce_mall_shipments
   - Verify shipment exists (404 Not Found if not found)
   - Verify shipment is not already delivered (check via ecommerce_mall_shipment_deliveries)
   - Reject with 409 Conflict if already delivered

3. Delivery Record Creation (Atomic Transaction)
   - Begin database transaction
   - Create delivery record in ecommerce_mall_shipment_deliveries:
     * shipment_id = shipmentId
     * customer_id = authenticated customer ID
     * delivered_at = current timestamp
     * is_auto_delivered = false (manual confirmation)
     * created_at = current timestamp
     * updated_at = current timestamp
   
   - Get all order items in this shipment:
     * Query ecommerce_mall_shipment_items by shipment_id
     * Get corresponding order items from ecommerce_mall_order_items
   
   - Update all order items status to 'delivered':
     * WHERE order_item_id IN (items from shipment)
     * SET status = 'delivered'
     * SET updated_at = current timestamp
   
   - Commit transaction

4. Return the created delivery record with shipment relationship

Error Handling:
- 404 Not Found: Shipment does not exist
- 403 Forbidden: Customer does not own the order for this shipment
- 409 Conflict: Shipment already delivered
- 422 Unprocessable Entity: Shipment in invalid state for delivery

Performance Considerations:
- Use database transaction to ensure atomicity
- Update all related order items in a single batch operation
- Create snapshot for audit (if required by snapshot policy)

operations.description:
Create a new shipment containing selected order items from the authenticated seller.

A shipment represents a physical package dispatched by a seller containing one or more order items. All items in a shipment must belong to the same seller (the authenticated user), belong to the same customer order, and share the same tracking information including carrier name and tracking number.

Upon successful creation:
- The shipment record is created with carrier and tracking information
- All selected order items are linked to this shipment via the shipment_items junction table
- All included order items simultaneously change status from 'paid' to 'shipped'
- The shipped_at timestamp is recorded

Sellers can only include their own order items with status 'paid' that are not yet shipped and have not been soft-deleted. Items from different sellers or different orders cannot be combined into the same shipment. The seller can choose to ship items individually in separate shipments or bundle multiple items together from the same order.

This operation is idempotency-unsafe and should not be retried without checking for existing shipments first.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Validate that the authenticated seller owns all specified order items. Query order items by the provided orderItemIds and verify all have status 'paid' and belong to the authenticated seller. If any item does not belong to the seller or is not in 'paid' status, return validation error. If order items belong to different orders, return error (all items in one shipment should ideally be from one order, though schema allows cross-order shipments via order_id field). Create shipment record with seller_id from session, order_id from first order item (all items should be from same order), carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at as current timestamp. Insert shipment_items records linking the shipment to each order item. Update all order item statuses from 'paid' to 'shipped'. Return the created shipment entity. Use database transaction for atomicity.

responseBody.description: The created shipment with full details including tracking information and associated order items

requestBody.description: Shipment creation request with selected order items to ship, tracking carrier name, and tracking number

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a specific shipment by its unique identifier.

This operation returns complete shipment details including the carrier name, tracking number, shipping timestamp, and all order items included in this physical package. The shipment items show which specific products and variants from the customer's order are contained in this shipment.

Shipments represent physical packages dispatched by sellers. Customers use this information to track delivery status using the carrier and tracking number. The response includes the seller information and associated order details for complete context.

Authorization ensures that only the customer who placed the order or the seller who created the shipment can view the details. Returns 404 if the shipment does not exist or has been deleted.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_shipments table by primary key id matching the shipmentId path parameter.

Include the following related data in the response:
- shipmentItems: Join with ecommerce_mall_shipment_items to get all items in this shipment
- For each shipment item, include the associated orderItem with product and variant details
- order: Include the parent order with customer shipping address information
- seller: Include seller profile information for the shipment sender

Validation rules:
- shipmentId must be a valid UUID format
- Shipment record must exist and not be soft-deleted (deleted_at is null)
- Return 404 NOT_FOUND error if shipment does not exist

Authorization checks:
- Customer must be the owner of the parent order (order.customer_id == current customer id)
- OR current user must be the seller who created the shipment (shipment.seller_id == current seller id)
- Return 403 FORBIDDEN if neither condition is met

Delivery status derivation:
- Check ecommerce_mall_shipment_deliveries table for delivery confirmation
- If delivery record exists or shipped_at + 14 days has passed, status is 'delivered'
- Otherwise status is 'in_transit'

Response must include derived 'status' field based on delivery confirmation state.

responseBody.description: Complete shipment details including tracking information, shipment items, and related order data

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the shipment to retrieve (UUID format)

Retrieve a paginated list of order snapshots for a specific order.

This operation provides access to historical snapshots of an order's state at various points in time. Order snapshots are automatically created during significant status changes and serve as immutable audit records for dispute resolution and order history tracking.

Customers can view snapshots of their own orders to track order progression. Sellers can view snapshots of orders containing their items. Administrators can view snapshots of any order on the platform for investigation purposes.

Snapshots include the complete order state at the time of capture, preserving all order item information, status, and related metadata. The response is paginated and supports filtering by snapshot creation time range.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query order snapshots filtered by the given orderId. Join with order_snapshots table where order_id matches the path parameter.

Apply optional filters from request body:
- createdAtFrom: filter snapshots created after this timestamp
- createdAtTo: filter snapshots created before this timestamp

Sort by created_at in descending order (newest first) by default.
Implement cursor-based or offset pagination based on request parameters.

Access control:
- Customers: can only view snapshots for their own orders
- Sellers: can only view snapshots for orders containing their items
- Administrators: can view snapshots for any order

Return paginated list of order snapshot summaries including snapshot ID, creation timestamp, and a summary of the order state at that point in time.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order snapshots for the specified order

operations.description:
Retrieve a single order snapshot by its ID.

Order snapshots are immutable records that capture a reference point of an order at a specific point in time. They are created automatically during significant order state changes or when audit records are required for compliance and legal purposes.

Each snapshot contains a reference to the order and the timestamp when the snapshot was captured. To view the complete order state at snapshot time, query the order data separately. Snapshots cannot be modified or deleted. This endpoint allows authorized users to view audit trail records for orders, supporting transparency and dispute resolution.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_order_snapshots table filtering by both snapshot_id and order_id to ensure the snapshot belongs to the specified order.

Return the complete snapshot record including: id, order_id, created_at, and any embedded order state data captured at snapshot time.

Authorization: Order owners (customers), order item sellers, and administrators can view snapshots. Verify the requesting actor has permission to access the parent order before returning snapshot data.

Edge cases: Return 404 if snapshot does not exist or does not belong to the specified order. Snapshots are immutable - no update or delete operations are supported.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of orders.

This operation provides order history browsing capabilities for customers and order management oversight for administrators. Customers can only view their own orders, while administrators can view all orders on the platform.

Orders can be filtered by various criteria including order status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, partially_completed), total price range, and creation date range. Results are paginated and support sorting by creation date, total price, and order number.

The response includes order summary information such as order number, total price, current status, and creation timestamp. For full order details including items, shipments, and address information, use the GET /orders/{orderId} endpoint.

Soft-deleted orders are excluded from results unless explicitly requested by administrators with appropriate permissions.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement order list query with the following logic:

**Authorization & Data Isolation:**
- For customers: Filter orders by authenticated customer's customer_id
- For admins: Allow viewing all orders, optionally filtered by specific customer
- Apply soft delete filter (exclude deleted_at IS NOT NULL unless admin with special permission)

**Query Implementation:**
- Base query on ecommerce_mall_orders table
- Join with ecommerce_mall_customers to get customer information for admin views
- Support the following filters in IRequest:
  - status: Filter by order status enum values
  - customerId: For admin use - filter to specific customer's orders
  - minTotalPrice/maxTotalPrice: Price range filtering
  - createdAfter/createdBefore: Date range filtering
  - orderNumber: Partial matching on order number for search

**Pagination:**
- Implement cursor-based or offset pagination based on request parameters
- Default page size: 20 items
- Maximum page size: 100 items
- Support sorting by: created_at (default, desc), total_price, order_number

**Response Construction:**
- Return IPageIEcommerceMallOrder.ISummary with:
  - data: Array of order summaries (id, orderNumber, totalPrice, status, createdAt)
  - pagination: cursor/limit/total information
- For ISummary DTO, include essential fields only (exclude full address details, those are in full entity)

**Performance Considerations:**
- Add database indexes on (customer_id, created_at) for customer queries
- Add index on status for filter performance
- Consider caching for frequently accessed order lists

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order summaries matching the search criteria

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering orders

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a specific order by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete order details including the order number, total price, shipping address, and overall order status. The response includes all order items with their product names, variant specifications, quantities, prices at time of purchase, and individual fulfillment statuses.

For each order item, the system preserves the purchase-time product and variant snapshots to ensure historical accuracy even if the original product data changes. Shipment information is included showing carrier names, tracking numbers, and which order items are included in each shipment.

Access control: Customers can only retrieve their own orders. Administrators can retrieve any order on the platform for oversight, support, and intervention purposes.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Retrieve order record from ecommerce_mall_orders table by orderId parameter.

Join with related tables to assemble complete response:
- ecommerce_mall_order_items for all items in the order, filtered by deleted_at IS NULL
- ecommerce_mall_order_item_product_snapshots for each item's product snapshot
- ecommerce_mall_order_item_variant_snapshots for each item's variant snapshot  
- ecommerce_mall_order_item_seller_snapshots for each item's seller profile snapshot
- ecommerce_mall_shipments for all shipments associated with this order
- ecommerce_mall_shipment_items to determine which items belong to each shipment

Authorization rules:
1. Extract authenticated user from session
2. If user is customer: verify order.customer_id matches authenticated customer id, else reject with 403
3. If user is admin or superAdmin: allow access to any order
4. If order.deleted_at IS NOT NULL: return 404 (order not found)

The order status is derived from item statuses following business rules:
- "paid" if all items are paid
- "shipped" if any item is shipped and none delivered
- "delivered" if all items are delivered  
- "cancelled" if all items are cancelled
- "refunded" if all items are refunded
- "partially_completed" for mixed states

Return full order entity with nested order items and shipments populated.

Sellers can view items for their products, filter by status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded), and manage their fulfillment workflow. operations.description:
Retrieves the immutable snapshot data for a specific order item.

This endpoint returns the complete purchase-time state captured when the order was placed, including:
- The product snapshot with name, description, category, base price, and images as they appeared at purchase time
- The variant snapshot with SKU code, option values, and price at the time of purchase
- The seller profile snapshot with shop name and logo as they were displayed to the customer

Snapshots are created automatically by the system during order creation and serve as the authoritative historical record for dispute resolution and legal compliance. They remain unchanged even if the original product, variant, or seller profile is later modified or deleted.

The snapshot data is used when displaying historical order information to ensure customers always see exactly what they purchased, regardless of subsequent changes to the seller's catalog or profile.
